You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob every path of your list. Drop a path that does not exist; never guess a prefix.

## Answer

Return filepaths and it's dependencies confirmed to be related to the task scope. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. **How I counted dropped.** A missed truth folder counts if its path appears as a substring in any navigator tool result. I got the same counts with and without the first result (the index read), so the index is not what inflates it. The substring match can still over-count a folder that only appears inside a longer path in a grep or glob result.

---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob every path of your list. Drop a path that does not exist; never guess a prefix.

## Answer

Return filepaths and it's dependencies confirmed to be related to the task scope. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. Paths are relative to the repository root: never copy the absolute working-directory part of a path a tool printed or you passed to it. Every path in the answer exists (checked in Stage C):

---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 3 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes. Every such folder goes into the answer, also outside the page or screen the ticket names; do not narrow the answer to one screen.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob every path of your list. Drop a path that does not exist; never guess a prefix.

## Answer

Return filepaths and it's dependencies confirmed to be related to the task scope. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. Paths are relative to the repository root: never copy the absolute working-directory part of a path a tool printed or you passed to it. Every path in the answer exists (checked in Stage C):

---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 3 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes. Every such folder goes into the answer, also outside the page or screen the ticket names; do not narrow the answer to one screen.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob every path of your list. Drop a path that does not exist; never guess a prefix.

## Answer

Return filepaths and it's dependencies confirmed to be related to the task scope. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. Paths are relative to the repository root: never copy the absolute working-directory part of a path a tool printed or you passed to it. Every path in the answer exists (checked in Stage C):

# Shared pipes
Root: main/pipes
## Purpose
- Pipes formatting units, translations, text casing and markdown for templates.
- Roles: unit pipes (UnitPipe, DisplayLoadWeightPipe), translate-* pipes over i18n keys, text pipes (KebabCase, SentenceCase, Markdown, TrustHtml).
## Key files
- display-distance.pipe.ts - DisplayDistancePipe
- index-as-letter.pipe.ts - IndexAsLetterPipe
- kebab-case.pipe.ts - KebabCasePipe
- markdown.pipe.ts - MarkdownPipe
- placeholder.pipe.ts - PlaceholderPipe
- report-estimated-time.pipe.ts - ReportEstimatedTimePipe
- sentence-case.pipe.ts - SentenceCasePipe
- split-camel-case.pipe.ts - SplitCamelCasePipe
- time.pipe.ts - TimePipe
- translate/translate-base.pipe.ts - TranslateBasePipe
- translate/translate-coupling-quality.pipe.ts - TranslateCouplingQualityPipe
- translate/translate-hand-side.pipe.ts - TranslateHandSidePipe
- translate/translate-hand-used.pipe.ts - TranslateHandUsedPipe
- translate/translate-sex.pipe.ts - TranslateSexPipe
- translate/translate-shoulder-side.pipe.ts - TranslateShoulderSidePipe
- translate/translate-unit-system.pipe.ts - TranslateUnitSystemPipe
- trust-html.pipe.ts - TrustHtmlPipe
## Folders
- translate/ - translate-base, translate-coupling-quality, translate-hand-side, translate-hand-used, translate-sex, translate-shoulder-side, translate-unit-system
- units/ - display-employee-height, display-employee-weight, display-load-weight, unit-force-value, unit
## Depends on
- main/models/units and ngx-translate.
## Gotchas
- unit pipes depend on the org UnitSystem setting, so output changes with it.
# How to navigate inseer-frontend
## How to read
- List index.md, open the one module note, Grep the name, then Read with offset and limit; never Read whole large files.
## Entry points
- main/main.ts - bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, appConfig)
- main/screens/app/app.component.ts - shell component with layout, nav header, banners
- main/screens/app/app.config.ts - global providers: router, HTTP interceptors, i18n, Material, Toastr, feature flags
- main/screens/app/app.routes.ts - APP_ROUTES with lazy children and guards
- main/screens/report/report.routes.ts - report page and per-tool wizard routes behind feature flags
## Where things live
- API services (stateless): main/services/*.service.ts and main/features/*/services
- DTOs and enums: main/models
- Feature flags: main/features/feature-flags/models/feature-flag.ts
- Global state facades: main/state/*.facade.ts
- Guards: main/guards; resolvers: main/resolvers
- HTTP interceptors: main/interceptors
- Org-scoped provider helpers: main/providers/org-scoped-providers.ts
- Score tool slices: main/features/score-types/<tool>
- Shared table: main/shared/modules/advanced-table
- Translations: main/assets/i18n/en.json

from ev2 import *
import collections
def neigh(ans_folders,both=True,topn=10,maxfan=60):
    seeds=[f for f in IMP.keys()|REV.keys() if os.path.dirname(f) in set(ans_folders)]
    sc=collections.Counter()
    for f in seeds:
        for g in (IMP[f]|(REV[f] if both else set())):
            d=os.path.dirname(g)
            if d in ans_folders: continue
            sc[d]+=1
    # downweight hub folders (many in-edges globally)
    hub=collections.Counter()
    for f,gs in IMP.items():
        for g in gs: hub[os.path.dirname(g)]+=1
    r={d:n/ (1+math.log(1+hub[d])) for d,n in sc.items()}
    return r
res=collections.defaultdict(list)
for arm,s,id,f in runs():
    if arm=='sonnet': continue
    calls,rs,a=load_run(f); ans=tf(parse_block(a)); t=truth(id)

        for n in (5,10,20):
            out=ans+top(nb,n); s_=score(t,out)
            res[(both,n)].append((id,s_['R']-base['R'],s_['P'],len(out)))

from ev import *
def render(id,N=20):
    tx=ticket(id); T=terms(tx)
    folder,fscore,tt=gen_a(tx)
    W={t:math.log(N_/len(hits(t))) for t in tt for N_ in [len(files)]}
    items=sorted(folder.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1])[:N]
    lines=[]
    for d,s in items:
        fs=[f for f in files if os.path.dirname(f)==d]
        hit=collections.Counter()
        for t in tt:
            for f in hits(t):
                if os.path.dirname(f)==d: hit[t]+=1
        best=sorted(hit,key=lambda t:-W[t])[:3]
        nf=len({f for t in hit for f in hits(t) if os.path.dirname(f)==d})
        lines.append(f"{d}/ - {nf}/{len(fs)} files; {', '.join(best)}")
    return '\n'.join(lines),items
if __name__=='__main__':
    toks=[]

**Result.** A deterministic ticket-terms-to-source-grep-to-folders tool (generator a) reaches the bare recall level only when its top 20 folders are unioned with haiku's own answer. On the 3 bench cases with haiku traces, the union gets R 0.50–0.54 against bare 0.51, at 30–40 folders. The tool alone fails on the two big-truth cases. Offline only, $0, no product edits, no git state commands. Scratch is in /tmp/navtool/ (lib.py, gen.py, ev*.py). The bench copy there is a scratch git repo, not the bench.

My re-score of haiku's own answer (the subagent hand-back) reproduces the aggregate R values exactly (for example 0.156). Haiku has traces on only 3 of the 10 cases (6141, 3571, 6404): 24 runs. The generators below ran on all 10 cases.

**Q1. Why haiku misses folders**

Mean recall per arm on the 3 traced cases:

| arm | R | P | folders | runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| haiku, all 4 prompt variants | 0.410 | 0.651 | 14.5 | 24 |
| haiku, current prompt (cap) | 0.445 | 0.609 | 15.3 | 6 |
| sonnet | 0.454 | 0.751 | 15.8 | 6 |
| bare, same 3 cases | 0.510 | 0.641 | | 9 |
| bare, all 10 cases | 0.530 | 0.543 | | 30 |

Missed truth folders per run, by class:

| arm | missed | never reached | context note listing only | source hit, dropped | parent named instead of child |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| orig | 23.7 | 70 of 142 | 18 | 33 | 21 |
| trim | 23.8 | 60 | 24 | 56 | 3 |
| cap | 20.8 | 71 | 8 | 12 | 34 |
| grep budget | 22.5 | 88 | 5 | 29 | 13 |
| sonnet | 20.3 | 94 | 6 | 6 | 16 |

The class cells are totals over the 6 runs of each arm. "Never reached" is a total of 142 misses for orig.

- **Most misses are never reached, and sonnet is no better.** Sonnet never reaches 26 of 45 folders on 6141 and 21 of 42 on 3571. Those two tickets name labels, not the components that render them (cv-backed-form-field, tag, card-button). Term search alone cannot get there.
- **Haiku reads notes instead of searching.** Orig and trim read 8 notes per run, cap reads 2.3, sonnet 0.8. Sonnet makes 8.2 source greps per run, 26 of them in `content` mode. Haiku makes 2.2–4.7 greps per run, nearly all `files_with_matches`.
- **Haiku truncates and wastes greps.** `head_limit` is set on 8 of 18 greps. In orig, 5 of 18 greps came back empty, partly from a nonexistent `src/` path.
- **Haiku drops what it found.** On 3571 it reached 13 folders (orig) and 25 (trim) by grep and left them out of the answer. The cap prompt cut this to 6, but it also lowered reach.
- **The cap prompt shifts misses into parent/child mismatch.** Parent-named-instead-of-child misses rose from 3 to 34. Sonnet has 16.

**Q2. Candidate generators, all 10 cases**

Setup:
- Source corpus: 3965 ts/html/scss/json files under `main/`.
- Terms: quoted strings, camel/kebab/snake identifiers, acronyms and non-stop words. Terms hitting more than 4% of files are dropped, the rest are IDF-weighted, and the top 60 are kept.
- Ranking: leaf folders by summed term weight.
- (b) greps the 2206 note lines and maps each to its `Folders` / `Key files` folder.
- (c) adds the import-graph neighbours (8907 edges) of the top-10 hit files.

| gen | candidates | ceiling R | top-10 R / P | top-20 R / P | top-30 R / P | tokens, top-20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a, source grep | 275 | 0.706 | 0.344 / 0.330 | 0.435 / 0.235 | 0.452 / 0.190 | 193 (path only) |
| b, notes | 137 | 0.539 | 0.139 / 0.100 | 0.239 / 0.117 | 0.342 / 0.117 | 163 |
| c, a plus hop | 286 | 0.706 | 0.307 / 0.320 | 0.428 / 0.230 | 0.452 / 0.177 | 193 |

- **a, extending the list.** Top-60 gives R 0.524 at P 0.147. Adding b's top 10 to a's top 20 gives R 0.477 (+0.04) at 27 folders.
- **a, per case.** R20 is 1.0 on 6404, 0.67 on 5948, 0.62 on 6406 and 0.55 on 6086. It is 0.17 on 3571 and 0.0 on 6141 (ceiling 0.18), and 0.13 on 6292 (only 3 usable terms).
- **b is weak.** Note lines are short and do not hold the ticket's strings.
- **c adds nothing as an automatic hop.** Seeds picked by hit score do not lead anywhere useful.
- **Hop seeded by haiku's confirmed folders works.** Appending the import-neighbour folders of haiku's own answer folders, 10 per case, gives:

| appended | R | P | folders |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 0.41 | 0.65 | 14.5 |
| 10 neighbours | 0.525 | 0.47 | 24.5 |
| 20 neighbours | 0.54 | 0.39 | 34.5 |

- **Two things I tried that did not help.** Rolling leaf hits up into ancestor folders did not help: R 0.452 to 0.452 at top-30, and 0.524 to 0.332 at θ=0.2. A grid over document-frequency cut-off, term count, multiplicity cap and weighting ranged R20 0.27–0.47, so I kept the simple default. Treat the 0.435 as having ±0.03 noise, since the grid was tuned on the same 10 cases.
- **Existing `map`, run for comparison.** I ran the existing `ambicode.mjs map` with the same top 10 terms in a scratch repo copy, with spec and mock files filtered out. It gave R 0.173, P 0.135, 16 folders and about 1500 tokens. It ranks files, not folders. This is not a like-for-like comparison, because map took 10 terms and my generator 60.

Simulated scored outcome, 24 haiku runs on the 3 traced cases, with candidates from generator a:

| answer | R | P | F1 | folders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| haiku alone | 0.410 | 0.651 | 0.480 | 14.5 |
| top-10 alone | 0.373 | 0.433 | 0.316 | 10 |
| top-20 alone | 0.389 | 0.300 | 0.239 | 20 |
| top-30 alone | 0.389 | 0.256 | 0.209 | 30 |
| haiku + top-10 | 0.498 | 0.496 | 0.451 | 21 |
| haiku + top-20 | 0.504 | 0.366 | 0.360 | 30 |
| haiku + top-30 | 0.504 | 0.305 | 0.316 | 40 |
| haiku + top-10 + 10 neighbours | 0.533 | 0.415 | 0.425 | 31 |
| haiku + top-20 + 10 neighbours | 0.540 | 0.347 | 0.372 | 40 |

By case, haiku + top-20 gives R 1.0 on 6404 (haiku alone 0.75), 0.37 on 3571 (0.34) and 0.14 on 6141 (0.14).

**Leakage.** The bench HEAD contains the solution. To measure it, I removed every ticket term whose hits all fall in truth or allowed files.
- Mean R20 went from 0.435 to 0.385. The drop comes from case 438 alone (0.50 to 0.00): its "Add new employee" string exists only post-change.
- The ceiling is unchanged (0.706, 0.728 after removal).
- So leakage costs about 0.05 R20, concentrated in one of 10 cases. Haiku's and sonnet's own greps are leaked in the same way.

**Q3. Recommendation: one CLI subcommand, plus haiku keeping its own answer**

- **Where it lives.** Extend `map` (`src/modules/search/map.ts`, `src/cli/commands/search/search.ts`) instead of adding a parallel command. `map` is file-oriented and needs the model to pick terms. Add `--folders` and ticket text on stdin (heredoc) with mechanical term extraction. An optional `--near <folder>...` flag returns the import-neighbour folders. Use a new `nav` name only if the `map` contract cannot bend.
- **Input and output.** It takes the ticket text and returns at most 20 folders, plus up to 10 `near` folders. I measured about 440 tokens (443 average over the 10 cases, 504 max, at chars/3.5). Example output, 6404, with the lines cut to the first 6:

```
main/assets/i18n/ - 15/16 files; view assessments, all assessments, showing
main/screens/upload/ - 4/5 files; all assessments, showing, redirect
main/services/ - 5/48 files; all assessments, logic, redirect
main/state/ - 4/25 files; redirect, instead, upload
main/features/amplitude/services/ - 2/2 files; all assessments, redirect, completed
main/screens/upload/manual-assessment/ - 3/4 files; all assessments, instead, upload
```

- **Prompt change.**
  1. Stage A is still reading `index.md`.
  2. Then one Bash call runs the tool on the ticket.
  3. Stage B opens at most 2 notes for the top modules.
  4. Stage C greps only for terms the evidence did not cover, in `content` mode, with no `head_limit`.
  5. The answer keeps every candidate with at least 2 distinct terms unless clearly unrelated, and ends with `--near` over the 3–6 confirmed folders.
  6. State "recall over precision, 25–30 folders OK". Drop the "name subfolders, never the parent" strictness, because the senior model filters.
  7. Delete the note-reading budget wording.
- **Tools.** `Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`, as `agents/scout.md` already has Bash.
- **Bash permission, verified.** `hooks/hooks.json` already routes `Bash(*ambicode.mjs*)` through the guard. `src/hook/guard/rules/output.ts` already auto-allows read-only `ambicode.mjs` calls, so a `nav`/`map` call can ride that rule.
- **Not verified.** I did not test whether frontmatter `tools: Bash(node:*)` works, because that needs a paid run.
  - The `claude` 2.1.303 binary documents `Bash(git *)` patterns only for `--allowedTools` and `--disallowedTools`.
  - Its `--tools` error says "a rule is not a tool name".
  - An agent frontmatter `disallowedTools:` field exists in a plugin bundled in the binary (claude-test).
  - Plan on plain `Bash`, restricted by the guard.
  - I also did not confirm that subagent Bash works under `dontAsk`.
- **MCP.** Not recommended: the plugin has no server process today, and the CLI route costs less.
- **Expected result.** Recall R 0.50–0.54, P 0.35–0.47, 25–40 folders, against bare 0.51 / 0.64 on the 3 traced cases (0.53 / 0.54 over 10). The union is what haiku gets if it keeps its own answer and adds all candidates. That is a recall upper bound, not a prediction of how haiku filters. F1 falls from 0.48 to about 0.37–0.45.
- **Risks.**
  - Huge cross-cutting tickets like 6141 stay near 0.14: the truth folders carry none of the ticket's words. Only `--near` helps there (+0.08 to +0.10).
  - Tickets with no identifiers (6292, 3 usable terms) stay near 0.13.
  - I did not measure runtime. A node file scan of about 4000 files should be fast but is unmeasured, and the document-frequency index would need caching.
  - The 10-case sample has high variance, and the tool's per-case ranking was only seen on those 10.

**Not done.**
- No paid haiku run with the tool in the loop. The union is simulated, not observed.
- I did not edit `map.ts`.
- I did not simulate the haiku-side filtering step.

My re-score of haiku's own answer (the subagent hand-back) reproduces the aggregate R values exactly (for example 0.156). Haiku has traces on only 3 of the 10 cases (6141, 3571, 6404): 24 runs. The generators below ran on all 10 cases.

**Q1. Why haiku misses folders**

Mean recall per arm on the 3 traced cases:

| arm | R | P | folders | runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| haiku, all 4 prompt variants | 0.410 | 0.651 | 14.5 | 24 |
| haiku, current prompt (cap) | 0.445 | 0.609 | 15.3 | 6 |
| sonnet | 0.454 | 0.751 | 15.8 | 6 |
| bare, same 3 cases | 0.510 | 0.641 | | 9 |
| bare, all 10 cases | 0.530 | 0.543 | | 30 |

Missed truth folders per run, by class:

| arm | missed | never reached | context note listing only | source hit, dropped | parent named instead of child |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| orig | 23.7 | 70 of 142 | 18 | 33 | 21 |
| trim | 23.8 | 60 | 24 | 56 | 3 |
| cap | 20.8 | 71 | 8 | 12 | 34 |
| grep budget | 22.5 | 88 | 5 | 29 | 13 |
| sonnet | 20.3 | 94 | 6 | 6 | 16 |

The class cells are totals over the 6 runs of each arm. "Never reached" is a total of 142 misses for orig.

- **Most misses are never reached, and sonnet is no better.** Sonnet never reaches 26 of 45 folders on 6141 and 21 of 42 on 3571. Those two tickets name labels, not the components that render them (cv-backed-form-field, tag, card-button). Term search alone cannot get there.
- **Haiku reads notes instead of searching.** Orig and trim read 8 notes per run, cap reads 2.3, sonnet 0.8. Sonnet makes 8.2 source greps per run, 26 of them in `content` mode. Haiku makes 2.2–4.7 greps per run, nearly all `files_with_matches`.
- **Haiku truncates and wastes greps.** `head_limit` is set on 8 of 18 greps. In orig, 5 of 18 greps came back empty, partly from a nonexistent `src/` path.
- **Haiku drops what it found.** On 3571 it reached 13 folders (orig) and 25 (trim) by grep and left them out of the answer. The cap prompt cut this to 6, but it also lowered reach.
- **The cap prompt shifts misses into parent/child mismatch.** Parent-named-instead-of-child misses rose from 3 to 34. Sonnet has 16.

**Q2. Candidate generators, all 10 cases**

Setup:
- Source corpus: 3965 ts/html/scss/json files under `main/`.
- Terms: quoted strings, camel/kebab/snake identifiers, acronyms and non-stop words. Terms hitting more than 4% of files are dropped, the rest are IDF-weighted, and the top 60 are kept.
- Ranking: leaf folders by summed term weight.
- (b) greps the 2206 note lines and maps each to its `Folders` / `Key files` folder.
- (c) adds the import-graph neighbours (8907 edges) of the top-10 hit files.

| gen | candidates | ceiling R | top-10 R / P | top-20 R / P | top-30 R / P | tokens, top-20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a, source grep | 275 | 0.706 | 0.344 / 0.330 | 0.435 / 0.235 | 0.452 / 0.190 | 193 (path only) |
| b, notes | 137 | 0.539 | 0.139 / 0.100 | 0.239 / 0.117 | 0.342 / 0.117 | 163 |
| c, a plus hop | 286 | 0.706 | 0.307 / 0.320 | 0.428 / 0.230 | 0.452 / 0.177 | 193 |

- **a, extending the list.** Top-60 gives R 0.524 at P 0.147. Adding b's top 10 to a's top 20 gives R 0.477 (+0.04) at 27 folders.
- **a, per case.** R20 is 1.0 on 6404, 0.67 on 5948, 0.62 on 6406 and 0.55 on 6086. It is 0.17 on 3571 and 0.0 on 6141 (ceiling 0.18), and 0.13 on 6292 (only 3 usable terms).
- **b is weak.** Note lines are short and do not hold the ticket's strings.
- **c adds nothing as an automatic hop.** Seeds picked by hit score do not lead anywhere useful.
- **Hop seeded by haiku's confirmed folders works.** Appending the import-neighbour folders of haiku's own answer folders, 10 per case, gives:

| appended | R | P | folders |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | 0.41 | 0.65 | 14.5 |
| 10 neighbours | 0.525 | 0.47 | 24.5 |
| 20 neighbours | 0.54 | 0.39 | 34.5 |

- **Two things I tried that did not help.** Rolling leaf hits up into ancestor folders did not help: R 0.452 to 0.452 at top-30, and 0.524 to 0.332 at θ=0.2. A grid over document-frequency cut-off, term count, multiplicity cap and weighting ranged R20 0.27–0.47, so I kept the simple default. Treat the 0.435 as having ±0.03 noise, since the grid was tuned on the same 10 cases.
- **Existing `map`, run for comparison.** I ran the existing `ambicode.mjs map` with the same top 10 terms in a scratch repo copy, with spec and mock files filtered out. It gave R 0.173, P 0.135, 16 folders and about 1500 tokens. It ranks files, not folders. This is not a like-for-like comparison, because map took 10 terms and my generator 60.

Simulated scored outcome, 24 haiku runs on the 3 traced cases, with candidates from generator a:

| answer | R | P | F1 | folders |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| haiku alone | 0.410 | 0.651 | 0.480 | 14.5 |
| top-10 alone | 0.373 | 0.433 | 0.316 | 10 |
| top-20 alone | 0.389 | 0.300 | 0.239 | 20 |
| top-30 alone | 0.389 | 0.256 | 0.209 | 30 |
| haiku + top-10 | 0.498 | 0.496 | 0.451 | 21 |
| haiku + top-20 | 0.504 | 0.366 | 0.360 | 30 |
| haiku + top-30 | 0.504 | 0.305 | 0.316 | 40 |
| haiku + top-10 + 10 neighbours | 0.533 | 0.415 | 0.425 | 31 |
| haiku + top-20 + 10 neighbours | 0.540 | 0.347 | 0.372 | 40 |

By case, haiku + top-20 gives R 1.0 on 6404 (haiku alone 0.75), 0.37 on 3571 (0.34) and 0.14 on 6141 (0.14).

**Leakage.** The bench HEAD contains the solution. To measure it, I removed every ticket term whose hits all fall in truth or allowed files.
- Mean R20 went from 0.435 to 0.385. The drop comes from case 438 alone (0.50 to 0.00): its "Add new employee" string exists only post-change.
- The ceiling is unchanged (0.706, 0.728 after removal).
- So leakage costs about 0.05 R20, concentrated in one of 10 cases. Haiku's and sonnet's own greps are leaked in the same way.

**Q3. Recommendation: one CLI subcommand, plus haiku keeping its own answer**

- **Where it lives.** Extend `map` (`src/modules/search/map.ts`, `src/cli/commands/search/search.ts`) instead of adding a parallel command. `map` is file-oriented and needs the model to pick terms. Add `--folders` and ticket text on stdin (heredoc) with mechanical term extraction. An optional `--near <folder>...` flag returns the import-neighbour folders. Use a new `nav` name only if the `map` contract cannot bend.
- **Input and output.** It takes the ticket text and returns at most 20 folders, plus up to 10 `near` folders. I measured about 440 tokens (443 average over the 10 cases, 504 max, at chars/3.5). Example output, 6404, with the lines cut to the first 6:

```
main/assets/i18n/ - 15/16 files; view assessments, all assessments, showing
main/screens/upload/ - 4/5 files; all assessments, showing, redirect
main/services/ - 5/48 files; all assessments, logic, redirect
main/state/ - 4/25 files; redirect, instead, upload
main/features/amplitude/services/ - 2/2 files; all assessments, redirect, completed
main/screens/upload/manual-assessment/ - 3/4 files; all assessments, instead, upload
```

- **Prompt change.**
  1. Stage A is still reading `index.md`.
  2. Then one Bash call runs the tool on the ticket.
  3. Stage B opens at most 2 notes for the top modules.
  4. Stage C greps only for terms the evidence did not cover, in `content` mode, with no `head_limit`.
  5. The answer keeps every candidate with at least 2 distinct terms unless clearly unrelated, and ends with `--near` over the 3–6 confirmed folders.
  6. State "recall over precision, 25–30 folders OK". Drop the "name subfolders, never the parent" strictness, because the senior model filters.
  7. Delete the note-reading budget wording.
- **Tools.** `Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`, as `agents/scout.md` already has Bash.
- **Bash permission, verified.** `hooks/hooks.json` already routes `Bash(*ambicode.mjs*)` through the guard. `src/hook/guard/rules/output.ts` already auto-allows read-only `ambicode.mjs` calls, so a `nav`/`map` call can ride that rule.
- **Not verified.** I did not test whether frontmatter `tools: Bash(node:*)` works, because that needs a paid run.
  - The `claude` 2.1.303 binary documents `Bash(git *)` patterns only for `--allowedTools` and `--disallowedTools`.
  - Its `--tools` error says "a rule is not a tool name".
  - An agent frontmatter `disallowedTools:` field exists in a plugin bundled in the binary (claude-test).
  - Plan on plain `Bash`, restricted by the guard.
  - I also did not confirm that subagent Bash works under `dontAsk`.
- **MCP.** Not recommended: the plugin has no server process today, and the CLI route costs less.
- **Expected result.** Recall R 0.50–0.54, P 0.35–0.47, 25–40 folders, against bare 0.51 / 0.64 on the 3 traced cases (0.53 / 0.54 over 10). The union is what haiku gets if it keeps its own answer and adds all candidates. That is a recall upper bound, not a prediction of how haiku filters. F1 falls from 0.48 to about 0.37–0.45.
- **Risks.**
  - Huge cross-cutting tickets like 6141 stay near 0.14: the truth folders carry none of the ticket's words. Only `--near` helps there (+0.08 to +0.10).
  - Tickets with no identifiers (6292, 3 usable terms) stay near 0.13.
  - I did not measure runtime. A node file scan of about 4000 files should be fast but is unmeasured, and the document-frequency index would need caching.
  - The 10-case sample has high variance, and the tool's per-case ranking was only seen on those 10.

**Not done.**
- No paid haiku run with the tool in the loop. The union is simulated, not observed.
- I did not edit `map.ts`.
- I did not simulate the haiku-side filtering step.

Бесплатный разбор по трейсам 24 прогонов haiku показал: детерминированный поиск по терминам тикета вместе с собственным ответом haiku поднимает recall до уровня bare. F1 при этом падает, потому что ответ разрастается. Это симуляция, а не прогон.

**Где теряет haiku.** Это 3 бенч-кейса, у которых есть трейсы haiku:

```
           R      P      папок  заметок/прогон  Grep/прогон
haiku      0.410  0.651  14.5   2.3–8           2.2–4.7
sonnet     0.454  0.751  15.8   0.8             8.2
bare       0.510  0.641
```

- **До большинства пропущенных папок не дошёл ни haiku, ни sonnet.** В 6141 и 3571 тикет называет надписи на экране, а не компоненты, которые их рисуют. Поиск по словам тикета до этих папок не доходит.
- **Ошибки самого haiku:**
  - читает заметки вместо поиска;
  - обрезает Grep через `head_limit`;
  - грепает несуществующий путь `src/`;
  - выбрасывает найденное: от 6 до 25 папок за прогон.

**Симуляция инструмента-кандидатов** на всех 10 кейсах:

```

haiku сам                             0.410  0.651  0.480  14.5
haiku ∪ топ-10 поиска по тикету       0.498  0.496  0.451  21
haiku ∪ топ-10 ∪ 10 соседей по импорт 0.533  0.415  0.425  31
bare (те же 3 кейса)                  0.510  0.641
```

- **Поиск по тикету:** термы из тикета механически, Grep по исходникам, папки ранжируются по попаданиям. Выдача около 440 токенов. Потолок recall 0.706, топ-20 даёт 0.435.
- **Соседи по импортам:** работают, только если стартовать от папок, которые haiku уже подтвердил. Автоматический переход от лучших попаданий ничего не даёт.
- **Утечка решения в HEAD бенча:** стоит около 0.05 recall, почти всё на кейсе 438.
- **Где инструмент не поможет:** очень широкие тикеты вроде 6141 и тикеты почти без идентификаторов (6292) останутся низкими.

**Предложение — один инструмент:**
1. **Код.** Расширить существующую команду `map` (`src/modules/search/map.ts`), а не заводить новую:
   - `--folders`: ранжирует папки, а не файлы;
   - тикет на stdin, термы извлекаются механически;
   - `--near <папки>`: соседи этих папок по импортам.
   - Тесты в том же изменении.
2. **Навигатор.** Получает `Bash` в дополнение к Read, Grep и Glob. Guard уже разрешает read-only вызовы `ambicode.mjs`, но в прогоне с сабагентом это ещё не проверено.
3. **Промпт.** Порядок: индекс → один вызов `map` по тикету → не больше 2 заметок → Grep только по непокрытым термам, без `head_limit` → `--near` от подтверждённых папок. Цель — recall важнее precision, ответ 25–30 папок.
4. **Проверка.** Бенч ×3: на ×2 у haiku разброс ±0.15. Около $0.6.

Ожидание по симуляции: recall примерно на уровне bare (0.50–0.54), precision ниже (0.4–0.5), стоимость почти не меняется, плюс один вызов CLI. Если вам важнее recall для старшей модели, это хороший размен. Если F1 — нет.

Делаем так?

1. `map --folders`, ticket text on stdin, or the existing terms input if map already takes terms.

     - quoted strings;
     - camelCase, kebab-case and snake_case identifiers;

`map --folders` and `map --near` are implemented and committed as 46f0d68f. On the 10-ticket bench the built CLI reproduces the prototype's recall: top-10 R 0.344 and top-20 R 0.435. No paid evals were run.

**Files changed**
- `src/modules/search/folders.ts` (new): term extraction, DF cutoff, IDF weighting, folder ranking, import graph and `--near`. It sits beside `map.ts`, `harvest.ts` and `refs.ts` as a sibling module.
- `src/cli/commands/search/search.ts`: `folders` and `near` flags added to `MAP_OPTIONS`, with a `runFolders` branch inside `runMap`. There is no new command.
- `src/modules/search/map.ts`: `STOPWORDS` is now exported and reused.
- Tests: `src/modules/search/folders.test.ts` (new, 7 tests) and one CLI-routing test added to `src/modules/search/search.test.ts`.

**Usage**
```
echo "<ticket>" | node scripts/ambicode.mjs map --folders        # or: map --folders --term "all assessments" (terms become quoted phrases)
node scripts/ambicode.mjs map --near main/screens/upload/ main/services/
```
`--json` also works. `--folders` output (6404):
```
main/assets/i18n/ - 15/16 files; all assessments, showing, redirect
main/screens/upload/ - 4/5 files; all assessments, showing, redirect
main/services/ - 4/48 files; all assessments, redirect, upload
```
`--near` output:
```
main/state/ - 15/25 files; imports given 29, imported by given 7
main/models/ - 13/23 files; imported by given 34
main/screens/report/services/ - 5/7 files; imports given 10
```

**Checks**
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm run build`: ok.
- `node --test` on `search.test.ts`, `map.test.ts`, `folders.test.ts` and `architecture.test.ts`: 25 pass, 0 fail. The architecture test is where the layer-import rule is checked.
- I did not run the full `verify` or `test:unit`.

**Offline bench**
The bench was `/tmp/navtool/bench` (a scratch copy), scored with the prototype's scorer through a new `/tmp/navtool/evcli.py`.

| | CLI | Prototype |
|---|---|---|
| top-10 R / P | 0.344 / 0.330 | 0.344 / 0.330 |
| top-20 R / P | 0.435 / 0.240 | 0.435 / 0.235 |

- **Runtime:** wall time is 1.63 s per call on average (max 2.7 s). That is mostly node startup plus reading about 4.7k files.
- **Output size:** about 440 tokens on average and 500 at most (chars/3.5).

**Decisions and open issues**
- **Corpus:** `map` does not exclude tests, so I mirrored that. The indexed files are everything git lists after `pathExclusionReason` and the project include/exclude globs, including html, scss, json and spec files. Using `map`'s `isSearchable` filter instead would drop html and scss, which the ticket terms match. I did not measure that variant.
- **Provenance:** the constants' comments cite the offline grid. The 20-line one reads "top-20 R 0.435, ceiling 0.706". The 4%, 60 and 10 comments only say "offline grid" with no per-constant number, because the prototype has no per-constant measurement for them.
- **Import graph:** it is regex-based and generic, resolving relative paths, Python `from ..x import`, extension-less paths, `index`/`__init__`/`mod`/`main` files, and unique path suffixes for non-relative specifiers. Test files are excluded from its edges. I tested it on the TS bench and on Python and TS fixtures, but not on other languages.
- **Ledger:** the new modes do not append a `map` ledger entry.
- **Stopwords:** the prototype's English stopword list is merged with the existing `STOPWORDS`.
- **Not done:** I did not run `map --near` against a bench ground truth, since there is none. It was only exercised on the bench by hand.

content.content:
1	---
2	name: navigator
3	description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
4	tools: Read, Grep, Glob
5	model: haiku
6	---
7	You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.
8	
9	## What you can read
10	
11	`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.
12	
13	## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)
14	
15	Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.
16	
17	Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.
18	
19	Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:
20	
21	`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`
22	
23	Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**
24	
25	## Stage B: notes
26	
27	Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 3 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.
28	
29	1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
30	2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
31	3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
32	4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
33	5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
34	   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
35	6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.
36

---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 3 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes. Every such folder goes into the answer, also outside the page or screen the ticket names; do not narrow the answer to one screen.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob every path of your list. Drop a path that does not exist; never guess a prefix.

---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it touches: the folders and files a change would edit. A senior model reads the code after you; it drops extras easily but rarely finds what you left out. Prefer recall: up to 30 paths is fine.

Bash is only for the two `map` calls below. Paths are relative to the repository root.

## 1. Map

Read `.ambicode/context/index.md` once, whole. It lists modules; a line's link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md` is the module's repo path. Note the modules the ticket belongs to.

## 2. Candidates

Run once, with the ticket text unchanged:

```
node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" map --folders <<'EOF'
<ticket text>
EOF
```

It prints up to 20 folders ranked by how many of the ticket's terms their files contain: `<folder>/ - <hit files>/<files> files; <matched terms>`.

## 3. Check

1. Open at most 2 notes (`.ambicode/context/modules/...`) for the modules from step 1 the candidates do not explain.
2. Grep the source for the ticket's distinctive strings (UI labels, keys, identifiers, routes) that neither the index nor the candidates cover: at most 4 Greps, `output_mode: content`, no `head_limit`, no path guessed (search from the root or from a folder you have seen).
3. Run once, with the 3 to 6 folders you are surest of:

```
node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" map --near <folder>/ <folder>/ ...
```

It prints up to 10 folders whose files import, or are imported by, files in those folders.

## Answer

- Every candidate folder with 2 or more matched terms, unless it is clearly unrelated to the ticket.
- Every folder your Greps hit that the ticket changes, also outside the page or screen the ticket names.
- `--near` folders the change would reach: shared components, services, state or models the ticket's behaviour runs through.
- Modules from the index the ticket names.

Name folders with a trailing `/`, files without. Copy paths exactly as a tool printed them, relative to the repository root: never the absolute working-directory part, never a prefix of your own, never a note path.

```files
<folder/ or file path> - a short reason
```

You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 3 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note decide which of it's sources belong to the ticket. Pick only sources that are missed and related to the task.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Filter the final list. Drop paths that clearly are out of scope. If you not sure, read a note about this item once, then decide.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes. Every such folder goes into the answer, also outside the page or screen the ticket names; do not narrow the answer to one screen.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob every path of your list. Drop a path that does not exist; never guess a prefix.

## Answer

Return filepaths and it's dependencies confirmed to be related to the task scope. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. Paths are relative to the repository root: never copy the absolute working-directory part of a path a tool printed or you passed to it. Every path in the answer exists (checked in Stage C):

```files
<folder/ or file path> -  a short description

## Context

`agents/navigator.md` (uncommitted, rewritten) is now on haiku with `tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`. It calls the bundled CLI twice:
- `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ambicode.mjs" map --folders <<'EOF' ... EOF`
- `... map --near <folders>`

`map --folders` and `map --near` were added in commit 46f0d68f.

In the navigator eval plugin arm, `evals/scripts/navigator-cases.mjs:200` sets `allowed_tools: [Agent]`. For `--tag navigator`, `evals/scripts/run.mjs` passes no `--allow-tools`. Cases cannot grant Bash themselves, so the navigator's Bash calls would be denied. The harness tool lists also bind subagents.

## Task 1: grant Bash to the plugin arm

1. Find how run.mjs grants tools to non-navigator cases (`--allow-tools Bash Edit Write` passed to `claude plugin eval`).
2. Find out whether that flag accepts a rule pattern, such as `Bash(node *)` or `Bash(node:*)`. Check `claude plugin eval --help` and try it cheaply if possible. A pattern is preferred because it keeps the main session from running arbitrary shell. If no pattern works, use plain `Bash`.
3. Grant it to the navigator plugin arm only. Bare stays `Read, Grep, Glob` with no Bash.
4. Update the run.mjs tests. Fix the stale comment in navigator-cases.mjs (lines ~59-61) if it is touched.
5. Regenerate the cases only if the generator changed:
   `NAV_BENCH=/Users/KillBill/Documents/projects/inseer/inseer-frontend npm run evals:generate`
6. Run `node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs` and `npm run build`.

## Task 2: smoke run

Run in the foreground, timeout 600000:
`npm run evals -- --tag navigator --case fe-vs-6404-navigator --runs 1 --max-cost-usd 0.5`

From the trace, verify:
- the navigator ran on haiku, per modelUsage;
- it called `map --folders` and got output, which means `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolved and the guard did not block it;
- it called `map --near`;
- the main session made no Bash, Read or Grep calls;
- the answer has no absolute paths.

If map fails (permission denied, an unresolved variable, or an error):
- Fix the eval tooling if that is the cause.
- If the cause is in `agents/navigator.md` (e.g. the command form), make the minimal fix there and say exactly what you changed.
- Re-run the smoke run. At most 2 smoke reruns.

## Task 3: bench

Do this only if the smoke run passed. Run sequentially, each as its own foreground command:
`npm run evals -- --tag navigator --case fe-vs-<id>-navigator --runs 3 --max-cost-usd 1`
for 6141, 3571 and 6404. Keep `find evals | wc -l` under 20000.

Per case, report:
- mean R / P / F1 and F1 per run;
- the answer path count;
- $/run, with the main and haiku split;
- navigator turns;
- Bash calls, and whether both map calls happened;
- missed/extra counts.

Comparison, haiku 634cccd3 (×2):

| case | F1 | R | P |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6141 | 0.144 | 0.156 | ~0.14 |
| 3571 | 0.616 | ~0.46 | 0.91 |
| 6404 | 0.744 | 0.714 | ~0.78 |

Bench mean R is about 0.445 (cap prompt) and F1 0.501. Bare: R 0.51, F1 0.558 (6141 0.339, 3571 0.521, 6404 0.815). Phase target: mean R ≥ 0.50 with at most about 30 paths.

## Commits

Make two commits, with these messages:
1. Eval tooling: `evals: grant Bash to the navigator plugin arm`
2. `agents/navigator.md`, whatever the result: `navigator: haiku with map --folders/--near candidates`

End each message with a blank line and `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

Report briefly:
- how Bash is granted (pattern or plain) and the evidence;
- the smoke checks;
- the bench table with stamps;
- the commits;
- any change you made to navigator.md.

def tf(items): return sorted({(i[:-1] if i.endswith('/') else os.path.dirname(i)) for i in items}-{''})
def truth(id):
    p=glob.glob(ROOT+f'navigator/*-{id}-navigator/truth.json')[0]
    return json.load(open(p))
def related(t,a,f):
    def acc(x):
        o=t['ancestors'].get(x); return o and o['total']>0 and o['relevant']/o['total']>=t['ancestorShare']
    return a==f or a.startswith(f+'/') or (f.startswith(a+'/') and acc(a))
def score(t,found):
    T=tf(t['relevant']); A=tf(found); ok=tf(t['relevant']+t['allowed'])
    missed=[f for f in T if not any(related(t,a,f) for a in A)]
    extra=[a for a in A if not any(related(t,a,f) for f in ok)]
    r=(len(T)-len(missed))/len(T); p=(len(A)-len(extra))/len(A) if A else 0
    f1=2*r*p/(r+p) if r+p else 0
    return dict(R=r,P=p,F1=f1,missed=missed,extra=extra,n=len(A))
def parse_block(text):
    m=re.search(r'```files\r?\n(.*?)```',re.sub(r'(?m)^ {2,4}','',text),re.S)
    if not m: return []
    out=[]
    for l in m.group(1).split('\n'):

Update Input Type Labels for REBA, RULA, and EST Wizard + Effort Details

**Summary:**  
Update input type labeling for **REBA**, **RULA**, and **EST** so that wizard fields, Scorecard Effort Details, shorthand indicators, and export resources use the new input type taxonomy: **AI**, **AI (overridden)**, **Calculated**, and **Manual**.

**Description:**  
As an ergonomist or safety professional completing or reviewing REBA, RULA, or EST assessments, I want all wizard and effort detail inputs to use consistent input type labels so that I can clearly understand whether a value was AI-generated, manually entered, calculated, or AI-generated and manually corrected.

This ticket applies to:

* **REBA:** Modal Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* **RULA:** Modal Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* **EST:** Single-Page Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* Export resources that display input type labels, including Share Report and other report/export outputs

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* REBA modal wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* RULA modal wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* EST single-page wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* REBA, RULA, and EST display “AI (overridden)” when a user manually edits an AI-generated value.
* Restore AI behavior reverts overridden AI values back to the original AI-generated value and changes the label back to “AI.”
* Manual values remain labeled as “Manual.”
* Calculated or derived values display as “Calculated” where applicable.
* REBA and RULA shorthand indicators and badges display “AI” for machine-generated inputs and “ai(o)” for AI-originated overridden values where shorthand is used.
* REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details display the updated input type taxonomy in the Input Type column.
* Export resources that include input type labels, including Share Report and other report/export outputs, use the same updated taxonomy.
* No user-facing wizard, Effort Details, shorthand indicator, or export label for these score types displays “Vision” or “CV.”
* All labels and shorthand indicators use the approved translation keys.

**Functional Requirements:**

* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-01:** The system shall display “AI” for all machine-generated REBA, RULA, and EST values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV,” regardless of whether the source is internal computer vision, internal ML, or external VLM.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-02:** The system shall display “AI (overridden)” when a user manually edits an AI-generated REBA, RULA, or EST value, and shall not display “AI (overridden)” for values whose original source was Manual or Calculated.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-03:** The system shall restore the original AI-generated value and display “AI” when the user selects Restore AI Values or equivalent restore behavior for REBA, RULA, or EST.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-04:** The system shall continue to display “Manual” for REBA, RULA, and EST values originally entered manually by the user.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-05:** The system shall display “Calculated” for REBA, RULA, and EST values that are derived or computed from other inputs, where applicable.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-06:** REBA and RULA shorthand indicators and badges shall display “AI” for machine-generated inputs and “ai(o)” for AI-originated overridden values where shorthand is displayed.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-07:** REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details shall display “AI,” “AI (overridden),” “Calculated,” or “Manual” in the Input Type column according to the target input type taxonomy.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-08:** REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details shall reflect the latest persisted assessment state after save, edit, restore, or page refresh.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-09:** Export resources that display input type labels for REBA, RULA, or EST, including Share Report and other report/export outputs, shall use the same updated input type taxonomy as Scorecard Effort Details.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-10:** The system shall use approved translation keys for REBA, RULA, and EST wizard and Effort Details labels, including `scorecard.input_type.ai`, `scorecard.input_type.manual`, `scorecard.input_type.calculated`, `scorecard.input_type.ai_overridden`, `scorecard.input_indicator.ai_short`, and `scorecard.input_indicator.ai_overridden_short`.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-11:** The system shall preserve source provenance separately from display labels where required to support override, restore, auditability, and future source-specific reporting.

**Out of Scope:**

* Changes to REBA, RULA, or EST scoring logic.
* Changes to AI, CV, ML, or VLM model outputs.
* Changes to calculation formulas.
* Broad scorecard layout redesigns beyond label and shorthand updates.
* NIOSH Proposals side-by-side layout updates.

**QA Notes:**

* Test REBA modal wizard, RULA modal wizard, and EST single-page wizard independently.
* Verify AI, AI overridden, Manual, and Calculated states.
* Verify restore behavior for overridden AI values.
* Verify REBA and RULA shorthand indicators.
* Verify Scorecard Effort Details after save, edit, restore, and page refresh.
* Verify Share Report and other export resources that display input type labels.
* Verify no “Vision” or “CV” labels remain for these score types.

**Result: the data-file hop does nothing for recall. Do not implement it in folders.ts.** On 6141 and 3571 it changes no number at all.

**Setup.** I wrote a Python port of `folders.ts` plus the hop, in /tmp/navtool/hop.py, hopeval.py and hop2.py. The scratch bench is filtered by the bench's config (`main/**`, helpPages and other excludes). The port reproduces the CLI closely, but not exactly:

| | Port, top-10 R | CLI, top-10 R | Port, top-20 R | CLI, top-20 R |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All 10 cases | 0.341 | 0.344 | 0.435 | 0.435 |

Per-case differences from the CLI are at most 0.02 R, plus 3571 top-20 P 0.65 vs 0.60. I did not chase them.

**Hop.**
- Data files are `json`, `yaml`, `yml`, `properties`, `po`, `toml`, `ini`, `arb`, `strings` and `xlf`.
- For each term that hits a data file, I take the keys of the entries whose value contains the term. JSON is parsed and flattened to dotted keys; other formats use a key:value regex.
- I grep the non-data files for the full dotted key, falling back to the last segment if it is at least 4 characters.
- The source files found credit their folders in place of the data-file hit. The "keep" variant credits both.
- K is the maximum number of matching keys per term. UCAP is the maximum number of usage files per key.

**All 10 cases, mean R and P (top-10 / top-20):**

| Config | Top-10 R | Top-10 P | Top-20 R | Top-20 P |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 0.341 | 0.330 | 0.435 | 0.245 |
| hop K6 U15 | 0.341 | 0.320 | 0.435 | 0.245 |
| hop K30 U40 | 0.363 | 0.310 | 0.435 | 0.245 |
| hop K30 U40, keep data folder | 0.341 | 0.320 | 0.435 | 0.255 |
| hop K200 U200 | 0.330 | 0.260 | 0.419 | 0.185 |

The best config, K30 U40 (top-10 R 0.363), is below noise. The wide K200 U200 setting is worse. I also ran K3, K12 and UCAP 8/15/40 variants (the first K3 and K6 rows in the earlier grid); none beat K30 U40.

**Per case, R at top-10 / top-20 and P at top-20.** Base is the first value in each cell. The K6 U15 row is identical to base on all of these cells. The K30 U40 row changes only 3571 top-20 P and 6404 top-20 P.

| Case | R top-10 | R top-20 | P top-20 (base, K30 U40) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6141 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.05, 0.05 |
| 3571 | 0.10 | 0.17 | 0.65, 0.60 |
| 6404 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 0.30, 0.25 |

**Why it fails.**
- On 6141 the label terms ("vision", "ai (overridden)", "calculated") do hit i18n keys: `common.vision`, `common.override`, `common.manual`, `common.calculated`.
- Those keys are used by 1 to 8 source files, and none of those files is in the truth folders. The files to change (cv-backed-form-field, effort details, wizards) don't reference these keys today. Their labels come through mapping layers, or are new keys the ticket adds.
- Most other data-file hits are generic words ("support", "calculation", "employee") that match 50 to 100 or more keys. That is noise, and it explains the P loss at wide K.
- On 3571 the same happens. "viewer" maps to `shared.edit_user_dialog.role_viewer`, whose users are not in the truth.

**Union with the navigator answer.** I could not identify which traces are 634cccd3 runs. The answer's stated model is the orchestrator, and no 634cccd3 label appears. I used the 14-15h plugin traces instead: 14-27 to 14-31 and 15-13 to 15-34 on 2026-10-20. Results are per run, as "answer R" then "answer + top-10 R":
- **6141** (6 runs): unchanged. 0.16→0.16, 0.20→0.20, 0.20→0.20, 0.18→0.18, and 0.00→0.00 for the other two. The hop adds nothing.
- **3571** (6 runs): +0.00 to +0.03 R. For example 0.40→0.43 and 0.38→0.38. P drops 0.03 to 0.15.
- **6404** (about 5 runs): answers sit at R 0.71 to 1.00. The union lifts the 0.71 to 0.86 runs to 1.00 (for example 0.71→1.00 and 0.86→1.00), at P 0.80→0.55.
- Hop and base unions are identical to within 0.01 R. The top-10 base list is itself worth almost nothing on 6141 and 3571.

**Leakage.**
- The truth commits for 6141, 3571 and 6404 are all ancestors of the real bench HEAD, so the bench snapshot is post-change.
- Since the hop gained nothing, no gain is inflated by post-change files.
- I did not look for post-change-only files that might have mattered. There are none that the hop found: neither `scorecard.input_type` nor `input_type.ai` exists anywhere under `main/`.

**Regeneration check of the 7 other cases.**
- I compared the current `recall-*` grader name sets in `evals/cases/navigator/*/graders` against the earliest 2026-10-20 aggregate-result.json for each case.
- All 10 cases match exactly, including 6141 (45), 3571 (42) and 6404 (7). The other seven are 438 (2), 5948 (9), 6292 (15), 5967 (16), 5164 (3), 6406 (8) and 6086 (11).
- I compared names only, not each grader's pattern text.
- The Downloads source `truth.json` is a different, larger raw list. It has `missingFromSnapshot` and 4 to 66 files per case, versus 2 to 45 relevant entries in the current files. The current `truth.json` is derived from it and is not byte-identical. I did not run the generator.

**Recommendation.** Do not add the hop to folders.ts. It adds code for zero recall gain, and it costs precision at any wider setting. The UI-copy failure is structural: the files to change are not reachable from the current copy by any key grep. 6141 and 3571 stay at R 0.00 to 0.17 with or without it. The haiku answer plus an unchanged top-10 list is the better path for those two.

Files: /tmp/navtool/hop.py, hopeval.py, hop2.py, hopgrid.py.

**Variant mapping (judged from commit times and tool behaviour; the trace does not record the navigator prompt)**
- 13-36..13-39 = sonnet 4c6c84ad, V2.1.
- 14-10..14-14 = 634cccd3. Haiku, Read/Grep/Glob.

## 1. Tool availability

**In the Bash-granted runs the subagent had no Grep or Glob.**
- The `init` entry lists only the main session's tools (Task, Bash, Read, Skill, TaskStop, ToolSearch). The subagent's own list is not recorded.

| | Grep | Glob |
|---|---|---|

| variant | 6141 | 3571 | 6404 |
|---|---|---|---|

  - Read index.
  - Grep context (`input type|effort detail|Share Report|overridden|Restore AI`).
