---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself: it drops an extra path in a second, but it never finds a path you left out. When unsure, keep the path. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 3 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note keep every source the ticket changes, and every source that uses or is used by what it changes. A note line naming a path is evidence enough: it needs no Grep or Glob to count.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Keep same-kind siblings. When you keep one subfolder of a kind (one per item, field, variant or step), keep every sibling of that kind the note lists, unless the ticket excludes it.
   Example: the ticket changes the unit shown in every detail panel; `panel/` lists `head-detail/`, `arm-detail/`, `leg-detail/`, `summary/`. Answer all three `*-detail/` folders, not only the one a Grep hit.
7. Drop only paths that are clearly unrelated to the ticket. When unsure, keep the path.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

1. Grep the source (`files_with_matches`) for the ticket's distinctive strings the notes did not resolve: UI labels, keys, constant or field names, routes. Add the folders of hits that the ticket changes. Every such folder goes into the answer, also outside the page or screen the ticket names; do not narrow the answer to one screen.
2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.
3. Glob only the paths you composed yourself, and drop one that does not exist; never guess a prefix. A path copied from a note line or a tool result exists: keep it without a Glob.

## Answer

Return every path you found related to the ticket, from the notes you read and from the Grep hits, with the dependencies the change reaches. A note line or a Grep hit is the evidence; a path needs no other confirmation. Name a folder (with a trailing `/`) only when every file inside it belongs to the ticket. Otherwise name the subfolders or files of it that do; never a parent folder in place of its children. Never name a note or a path with a parenthesis. Write each path exactly as its note's `Root:` line (plus the file or folder inside it) or its index link gives it; add no prefix of your own. Paths are relative to the repository root: never copy the absolute working-directory part of a path a tool printed or you passed to it. Every path in the answer was printed by a note or a tool, or checked by Glob in Stage C:

```files

Промпт навигатора поправлен, бенч запущен; результатов пока нет. Основа — `634cccd3`, лимит заметок вернул на 3. Все правки бьют в одну проблему: haiku срезает собственные находки.

1. **Правило доказательства вместо «confirmed».**
   - Answer: «Return every path you found related to the ticket, from the notes you read and from the Grep hits… A note line or a Grep hit is the evidence; a path needs no other confirmation.»
   - Требование «Every path exists (checked in Stage C)» заменено на «printed by a note or a tool, or checked by Glob».
2. **Glob только для путей, которые он собрал сам.** Путь из заметки или из вывода инструмента считается существующим. Это прямо отвечает на его же объяснение «not globbed, so they are left out».
3. **B2.** Было «Pick only sources that are missed and related». Стало: оставлять всё, что тикет меняет, и всё, что использует изменяемое или используется им. Строка заметки — достаточное доказательство.
4. **Новое: однотипные соседи** с коротким общим примером: три папки `*-row/` в настройках уведомлений, взять все три, а не одну, на которую попал Grep. Это закрывает случай на 6141, где haiku назвал 2 из 6 папок `*-detail`.
   - Первый вариант примера был слишком похож на кейс 6141 (`*-detail`), заменил его на нейтральный.
5. **Фильтр B6.** Теперь выбрасывать только явно не связанное, при сомнении оставлять. В начале промпта добавлено объяснение: планировщик лишнее выбросит за секунду, а пропущенное не найдёт никогда.

## Current version

0.6.0 (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, not bumped). Branch `navigator-agent`; commit after every phase/iteration (user, 2026-10-19).
Bench context = `inseer-frontend/.ambicode/context`, backup `.local-docs/context` (never touch; `cmp` index.md after every run).
`node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs` 73 pass, search tests 22 pass, typecheck clean (2026-10-20). `npm run verify` not run since the navigator work.

## Navigator: where we are (2026-10-20)

User decisions: the navigator stays on **haiku** (frequent scope subagent for all skills; a senior model refines; ±0.1 F1 vs sonnet is fine),
packaged as one tool, **no Bash** (too risky). Context exists only to make the navigator faster/cheaper; dropping it is a later decision.
Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plans: parent "navigator eval" (3146e432, phase p11) → child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397, p2 in progress).

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

```
variant                              6141   3571   6404   mean   R mean
bare (sonnet, no context)            .339   .521   .815   .558
sonnet V2.1 (4c6c84ad)               .33    .58    .86    .59
haiku 634cccd3 (cap 3 notes)         .144   .616   .744   .501   .443
haiku + map --folders/--near c46d76ae .050  .374   .738          .427
haiku 634 + map union 3d15eb34       .077   .355   .745          .356
haiku no context 4fef362f            .140   .465   .835   .480   .428
haiku cap 12 notes d5349924          .112   .536   .817   .488   .392
```

10 cases: bare R .530 P .543 F1 .505 $0.144; sonnet V2 F1 .518; sonnet V2.1 F1 .542 $0.128; context-only sonnet (pre-V2) F1 .396.

### Findings

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.
- Haiku obeys numeric caps and step order (6/6), not floors ("use all N": 3/6) or print steps (0/21). It emits no text/thinking.
- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.
- ~80% of haiku's lost truth folders never appear in a read note; sonnet reaches them by iterating source Greps (~10 on 6141).
- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.
- Bench cost: ~$0.55 per variant (3 cases x3); the sonnet relay main session dominates.

### In progress

Evidence-rule variant on 634cccd3 base, notes cap 6: "a note line or a Grep hit is evidence", Glob only self-composed paths,
B2 keep changed + users/used-by, same-kind siblings rule with a generic example, drop only clearly unrelated, recall framing.
Bench 3 cases x3 running; key metric is the funnel (named/listed, named without source hit).

## Next step

1. Report the evidence-rule bench; if the funnel moves toward sonnet without collapsing P, 10 cases x2.
2. Then: source-search iteration like sonnet (next Grep from the previous hits); decide on the context (user, later).
3. p12: dead code (learn/seed/`navigator` CLI), `npm run verify`, version bump.

## Eval setup (navigator)

- Cases `fe-vs-<id>-navigator`, generated by `evals/scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (gitignored); never run `evals:generate`
  without `NAV_CASES`/`NAV_BENCH` (it wiped the cases once; regenerated, grader names match for all 10).
- Run: `npm run evals -- --tag navigator --case fe-vs-<id>-navigator --runs N --max-cost-usd X`, one case per command, build first.
- Plugin arm: sonnet relay main session (`allowed_tools: [Agent]`) calls `ambicode:navigator` once. `run.mjs` strips
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL*` from the child env (the user's shell forces sonnet otherwise). Scaffold copies context + config.yaml.
- Scoring: truth/answer collapsed to folders, ancestorShare 0.3; metrics in `results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`.
- Eval dir must stay under 20,000 entries (18,433 at last count; ~16-30 per case run).
- Bench leakage: inseer-frontend HEAD is after every truth commit (favours source search for all arms).

## Open

- Dead learn/seed code and `navigator` CLI commands in `src/`; USAGE help-line cleanup.
- Path-prefix tolerance in the scorer (bare answers without `main/` score 0) — not decided.
- `skill-content` error-code test on navigator-* codes failing earlier; not checked against unmodified code.

## Task-lifecycle (older)

Done 2026-10-17 on `new_tuning` (run-3 audit fixes, verify green). Still open:
- plan-quality fails ~1 of 3 per plan case (judge reads the rubric literally); proposed rubric fix awaits the user.
- review-subtle unstable; rules-migrate rules-faithful 1 of 3; plan-reuse anchors-valid failed once.
- `agent_type` reaching the guard is not observed; if absent, the reviewer rule fails open.
- Linked requirements not passed to the review (~+28 KB): awaiting the user.
- plan-check is structural only; scout notes are thin (Depends on 0, Gotchas 0).
- VS Code started inside a Claude session inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`; start VS Code fresh.

40	- `graders/<name>.md`: frontmatter `type`, `weight` (default 1), `arm` (with-only | both), plus the options below. Types:
41	  - regex: pattern (JS regex), flags (e.g. i), match (contains | not_contains | "count:N"), target.
42	  - tool_used: tool, input_match (regex over the JSON input), min (default 1), max; never called = min 0 and max 0. A `Skill` check: tool: Skill, input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?<skill-name>"'.
43	  - tool_order: before, after (tool name or {tool, input_match}).
44	  - file_exists: path (glob of files Claude created), exists (default true).
45	  - llm: criteria (the file body), focus; concrete PASS/FAIL conditions, short outputs only.
46	  - baseline: baseline_file (.jsonl in the case dir), criteria.
47	- target (regex) and focus (llm): last_message (default) | trace | files (created paths) | { source: file, path: <file in workspace after the run> } | mock_calls.
48	- MCP mocks: `evals/mocks/<server>/<tool>.md` (or the case's own `mocks/`): body = tool result, with {{input.<field>}}; frontmatter type (fixed | agent), expect, error. A tool without a mock is unavailable.
49	- Prefer one grader on the result and one on the steps (tool_used/tool_order); use regex over llm whenever possible.
50	
51	# Reporting
52	After each phase or task tell the user briefly: what changed (files), how it was verified (eval result or check), what is left or uncertain, and the proposed next step. If something failed or was skipped, say so plainly.

# Role
You are the master agent of plugin-master: you develop the Claude Code plugin in the current working directory (the space) together with the user. You own the idea and the state of the plugin, drive the work through plans and subagents, and check the result with evals.

Your context is valuable: spend it on decisions, not on bulk work. You may read files (Read, Glob, Grep) and make small, well-understood edits yourself (Edit, Write): one file or a few lines, a wording fix, a version bump, a note in STATE.md. Anything larger, anything that needs searching across many files, research, running commands (Bash, web fetches and the like are blocked for you), multi-file changes and reviews goes to a subagent with the Agent tool. Plan, review short reports, ask the user and use the mcp__plan__* and mcp__evals__* tools. Reply in the language the user writes in; keep code, files and commit messages in English unless the plugin is meant for another language.

- `.plugin-master/DECISIONS.md`: one short entry per non-obvious decision (what, why, rejected alternatives). A subagent creates it when the first decision is made.
- Files under "# plugin-master context" below are already loaded in your prompt: do not read them again unless they may have changed during this session.
- This prompt itself is `.plugin-master/MASTER.md`: the user edits it, and a change applies to the next new session. Do not edit it unless the user asks.
- The plugin itself (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `skills/`, `commands/`, `agents/`, `hooks/`, `.mcp.json`) and its evals (`evals/`) are the product. Everything else in `.plugin-master/` is bookkeeping.

# Plans
Work is organized in plans with phases, managed only through the mcp__plan__* tools (never edit `.plugin-master/plans/` by hand).
- At the start of every task call plan_get. If there is no active plan, the user chose to work without one: do the task directly and do not create or activate plans unless the user asks (for a large task you may suggest one once).
- If the active plan has no phases, propose 3-7 concrete phases with plan_set_phases. A phase is a verifiable step ("Skill X handles case Y, eval Z passes"), not an activity ("research").
- Before a phase call phase_start; after it call phase_complete with a one or two sentence summary of what changed and how it was verified. Record notable findings and decisions with plan_log.
- If a phase turns out to need several steps of its own, call plan_start_child for it. When the child plan is done call plan_complete and continue with the parent plan's next phase.

Cap-6 haiku runs are done. 6141 got worse (F1 .140 vs .144 for H634), 3571 and 6404 are mixed, and the mean F1 is .497 against .501 for H634 (about flat). The funnel improved but 6141 recall is still very low.

**Commits** (both include the Opus 5.5 Co-Authored-By line)
- 129c0ce is the evidence-rule version. The cap-6 correction arrived after this commit, so the cap-6 edit is a separate commit.
- 4fc7b3f is "navigator: open at most 6 notes".
- I rebuilt before every run.

**Diff vs 634cccd3 (`agents/navigator.md`; the cap-3 → cap-6 change is in 4fc7b3f, not in this diff):**
- The intro now says the planner drops an extra path in a second but never finds a missing one, so when unsure the navigator should keep the path.
- Stage B step 2: keep every source the ticket changes plus its users and used-bys. A note line naming a path is enough evidence, with no Grep or Glob needed.
- New step 6 on same-kind siblings: if you keep one, keep all siblings the note lists, with an example. The old step 6 became step 7: drop only clearly unrelated paths, keep when unsure.
- Stage C: Glob only the paths you composed yourself. A path copied from a note or a tool result is kept without a Glob.
- Answer: "confirmed" is replaced by "a note line or a Grep hit is the evidence". Paths must be printed by a note or a tool, or checked by Glob.

**Cap 6 (main table, 3 runs per case)**

| case | R | P | F1 | total $/run | answer chars (per run) | notes read | ctx Greps | src Greps | Globs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6141 (17-23-05-313) | .134 | .186 | **.140** | .086 | 3811 / 5203 / 4701 | 6 / 6 / 6 | 0 / 1 / 1 | 4 / 4 / 4 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| 3571 (17-24-58-997) | .397 | .842 | **.537** | .055 | 5312 / 2432 / 4824 | 6 / 6 / 3 | 1 / 1 / 2 | 2 / 1 / 1 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| 6404 (17-26-44-121) | .809 | .822 | **.815** | .039 | 2737 / 2144 / 2470 | 2 / 2 / 2 | 2 / 1 / 1 | 2 / 2 / 4 | 0 / 0 / 0 |

- The mean F1 over the three cases is .497, against .501 for H634.
- The navigator ran on claude-haiku-5-5 in every run. Each run's modelUsage also lists claude-sonnet-5-5, which is the parent session.
- The "src Reads 0" count is from the trace script. Run 3 on 3571 did one source Read.

**Cap 3 (stamp 2026-10-20T17-21-02-886Z, 6141 only; the other two cases were not started)**
- R .178, P .198, F1 .187, $.087 per run.
- Notes read 3 / 3 / 3, src Greps 3 / 4 / 3, Globs 0.

**Funnel** (truth folders listed in a note the navigator read; cap 6, n=9 runs)
- Named / listed: 26/36 = **0.72**.
  - Previous values: haiku V2.1 0.47, H634 0.60, sonnet 0.77. Cap 3 on 6141 alone was 6/6.
- P(named | source hit) = 21/22 = **0.95**. Sonnet was 0.94.
- P(named | no source hit) = 5/14 = **0.36**. Haiku V2.1 was 0.09, so this is up, but sonnet's was higher.
  - Of the 10 unnamed truth folders, 8 had a sibling from the same note named and 2 had no sibling named. These come from the q5-style tally, which classifies them.
- Kept rate of non-truth note folders:
  - q3 tally: 31 of 146, **0.21**. Cap 3 was 19 of 46 (0.41), a small sample.
  - q5 tally: 36 of 160, 0.23.
  - Previous: haiku 0.08-0.21, sonnet 0.14.
- Precision of the kept note folders is 0.32, against 0.72 for sonnet and 0.36 for H634.

**Compliance**
- **Globs:** 0 in all 12 runs, against a mean of 2.2 for H634. The "Glob only composed paths" rule is followed, and the navigator now skips Glob entirely.
- **Siblings on 6141 (`*-detail`):**
  - In the one cap-6 run that read the effort-detail note, 22 `*-detail` folders were listed and only 6 were named. 11 of the 22 were truth, and 4 of those 11 were named.
  - The other two cap-6 runs read no `*-detail` note.
  - In the cap-3 run that read it, all 10 listed were named, 6 of them truth.
  - So the sibling rule was followed only in the cap-3 run, not in the cap-6 run.
- **6141 stage A:** the navigator mostly misses the right module. In the cap-6 runs, exact module precision was .06 and recall .04.

**Checks and cost**
- `cmp` of `inseer-frontend/.ambicode/context/index.md` against `.local-docs/context/index.md`: identical. I did not touch `.local-docs`.
- The evals dir has about 1,530 entries (`find -maxdepth 6`), well under 20,000.
- Cost: 4 runs of 3, roughly $0.087×3 + $0.086×3 + $0.055×3 + $0.039×3 = about $0.80 total. That includes the cap-3 run and is above the ~$0.55 budget. The cap-6 runs alone cost about $0.54.
- No commits touched `.plugin-master/` or `evals/cases/results/`.

**Open issues**
- On 6141 the navigator still reads the wrong notes, so recall is about .13. The cap change does not fix that; stage A module choice is the cause.
- Cap 6 lowered 6141 F1 against cap 3 (.140 vs .187), but cap 3 is one run set, so treat that as noise-level.

  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.

  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.

- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.

  `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL*` from the child env (the user's shell forces sonnet otherwise). Scaffold copies context + config.yaml.

Update Input Type Labels for REBA, RULA, and EST Wizard + Effort Details

**Summary:**  
Update input type labeling for **REBA**, **RULA**, and **EST** so that wizard fields, Scorecard Effort Details, shorthand indicators, and export resources use the new input type taxonomy: **AI**, **AI (overridden)**, **Calculated**, and **Manual**.

**Description:**  
As an ergonomist or safety professional completing or reviewing REBA, RULA, or EST assessments, I want all wizard and effort detail inputs to use consistent input type labels so that I can clearly understand whether a value was AI-generated, manually entered, calculated, or AI-generated and manually corrected.

This ticket applies to:

* **REBA:** Modal Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* **RULA:** Modal Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* **EST:** Single-Page Wizard + Scorecard Effort Details
* Export resources that display input type labels, including Share Report and other report/export outputs

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* REBA modal wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* RULA modal wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* EST single-page wizard displays “AI” for all machine-generated values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV.”
* REBA, RULA, and EST display “AI (overridden)” when a user manually edits an AI-generated value.
* Restore AI behavior reverts overridden AI values back to the original AI-generated value and changes the label back to “AI.”
* Manual values remain labeled as “Manual.”
* Calculated or derived values display as “Calculated” where applicable.
* REBA and RULA shorthand indicators and badges display “AI” for machine-generated inputs and “ai(o)” for AI-originated overridden values where shorthand is used.
* REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details display the updated input type taxonomy in the Input Type column.
* Export resources that include input type labels, including Share Report and other report/export outputs, use the same updated taxonomy.
* No user-facing wizard, Effort Details, shorthand indicator, or export label for these score types displays “Vision” or “CV.”
* All labels and shorthand indicators use the approved translation keys.

**Functional Requirements:**

* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-01:** The system shall display “AI” for all machine-generated REBA, RULA, and EST values, including values previously labeled “Vision” or “CV,” regardless of whether the source is internal computer vision, internal ML, or external VLM.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-02:** The system shall display “AI (overridden)” when a user manually edits an AI-generated REBA, RULA, or EST value, and shall not display “AI (overridden)” for values whose original source was Manual or Calculated.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-03:** The system shall restore the original AI-generated value and display “AI” when the user selects Restore AI Values or equivalent restore behavior for REBA, RULA, or EST.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-04:** The system shall continue to display “Manual” for REBA, RULA, and EST values originally entered manually by the user.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-05:** The system shall display “Calculated” for REBA, RULA, and EST values that are derived or computed from other inputs, where applicable.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-06:** REBA and RULA shorthand indicators and badges shall display “AI” for machine-generated inputs and “ai(o)” for AI-originated overridden values where shorthand is displayed.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-07:** REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details shall display “AI,” “AI (overridden),” “Calculated,” or “Manual” in the Input Type column according to the target input type taxonomy.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-08:** REBA, RULA, and EST Scorecard Effort Details shall reflect the latest persisted assessment state after save, edit, restore, or page refresh.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-09:** Export resources that display input type labels for REBA, RULA, or EST, including Share Report and other report/export outputs, shall use the same updated input type taxonomy as Scorecard Effort Details.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-10:** The system shall use approved translation keys for REBA, RULA, and EST wizard and Effort Details labels, including `scorecard.input_type.ai`, `scorecard.input_type.manual`, `scorecard.input_type.calculated`, `scorecard.input_type.ai_overridden`, `scorecard.input_indicator.ai_short`, and `scorecard.input_indicator.ai_overridden_short`.
* **FR-AI-LABEL-COMBO-11:** The system shall preserve source provenance separately from display labels where required to support override, restore, auditability, and future source-specific reporting.

**Out of Scope:**

* Changes to REBA, RULA, or EST scoring logic.
* Changes to AI, CV, ML, or VLM model outputs.
* Changes to calculation formulas.
* Broad scorecard layout redesigns beyond label and shorthand updates.
* NIOSH Proposals side-by-side layout updates.

**QA Notes:**

* Test REBA modal wizard, RULA modal wizard, and EST single-page wizard independently.
* Verify AI, AI overridden, Manual, and Calculated states.
* Verify restore behavior for overridden AI values.
* Verify REBA and RULA shorthand indicators.
* Verify Scorecard Effort Details after save, edit, restore, and page refresh.
* Verify Share Report and other export resources that display input type labels.
* Verify no “Vision” or “CV” labels remain for these score types.

input.message:
Haiku's main failure on 6141 is that it opens parent overview notes and runs out of its 6-note cap before it reaches the notes that list the truth folders. It does not pick the wrong area. Scripts are /tmp/navsteps/truth.mjs, mine1.mjs, mine2.mjs and mine3.mjs. mine1 prints per-run call sequences. mine3 counts opened notes that hold truth folders. Run them with node. Nothing in the repo was touched.

**1. Truth map (45 truth folders)**

The index is a nested tree, so one index line per note. A deeper note costs one Read, not one hop through parents.

| Group | Folders | Where it sits | Reads from index.md |
|---|---|---|---|
| reba and rula `score-card/effort-detail/*-detail` | 11 | `## Folders` bullet in the effort-detail note, which has its own index line (depth 4 under rula-reba) | 1 |
| reba `shared/{leg-position,upper-arm,wrist}` | 3 | `## Folders` bullet in reba/components (index line) | 1 |
| reba and rula `manual-override-wizard/{neck,trunk,lower-arm...}` | 7 | **absent**. The note lists only `manual-override-wizard/`, so these exist only in source. | none |
| rula-reba/shared `display-card`, `dotted-row` | 2 | **absent** from the note (index line exists). Only `models` (1) is listed. | none |
| lm-carry, lm-lift, lm-lower and rsi `manual-override-wizard/effort` | 4 | **absent** from the notes. lm-* have an index line; rsi has none. | none |
| est `score-card/shared/{cv-backed-metric,posture-scale-display}` | 2 | `## Folders` bullet in est/components/score-card (index line) | 1 |
| est wizard folders | 6 | `## Folders` bullet in the est wizard notes. These notes have **no index line**. They are reached through the `## Submodules` list in the est/components overview. | 3 or more (est, est/components, wizard) |
| ge-adv `card-set-display`, `expandable-card-display`, `card-checkbox-set`, `card-radio-button`, `expandable-card-checkbox` | 5 | `## Folders` bullet in a `shared` note (index line) | 1 |
| `components/inputs/cv-backed-form-field`, `ui/card-button`, `ui/tag` | 3 | `## Folders` bullet in an index-line note | 1 |
| `ui/tagged-metric` | 1 | absent from the ui note | none |

Totals: 31 folders are listed as a bullet inside a note (25 in notes with an index line, 6 in the est wizard notes without one). 14 are absent from every note, so no navigation of the context can name them.

**2. Ticket words against index lines**

- **REBA, RULA, EST:** these appear on the product index lines. Examples are "REBA services (API, scoring, forms...) and models", "REBA wizard inputs for neck, trunk, upper and lower arm...", "EST ergonomic screening...", and "Per-effort detail breakdown of REBA scores".
- **"Effort Details":** it maps to the `effort-detail` index lines for reba and rula. Those lines also hold 11 truth folders.
- **"Modal Wizard" and "Single-Page Wizard":** they map to the `components` lines ("wizard inputs"). They do not map to the manual-override-wizard sub-folders, which the notes omit.
- **"Input Type", "Share Report", "Vision/CV", "shorthand", "ai(o)":** none of these appear on a truth-module index line. Only the Vision/CV hook reaches the lateral modules (est cv-backed, ge-adv card sets, lm-*, ui/tag), and only through key symbols such as `ESTCVBackedMetricComponent`.
- **Share Report:** it matches the report-sharing dialogs line, which is off truth.

**3. Haiku and sonnet runs on 6141**

Notation: `+` is a note on a path to truth (an ancestor of a truth folder), `-` is off. The arrow in each Grep entry gives the number of context hits.

**Cap-6, stamp 17-23-05 (F1 .126, .157, .137):**

| Run | Context Grep | Notes opened, in order |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | none | +rula-reba, +est, +reba, +rula, -shared/components, -shared/services |
| 2 | `input type\|input_type\|Input Type\|overridden\|shorthand\|Share Report\|export\|ai\(o\)` → 13 hits, all on scoring-models, directives, models, screens/report, dialogs and nom | +rula-reba, +reba, +rula, +est, -shared, -screens/report |
| 3 | `input.?type\|shorthand\|ai\(o\)\|ai_overridden\|share report\|effort.detail` → 20 hits, including the two effort-detail notes | +rula-reba, +reba, +rula, +est, +reba effort-detail, +rula effort-detail |

All three runs then spent 3-4 source Greps on i18n keys and `isRebaCvChecked`.

**Cap-3, stamp 17-21-02:**

| Run | Context Grep | Notes opened |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `input.?type\|input_indicator\|overrid\|Share Report...` → 53 hits | +reba, +rula, +est |
| 2 | `input type\|overridden\|shorthand\|effort-detail...` → 19 hits, including the effort-detail notes | +rula-reba, +est, +reba effort-detail |
| 3 | none | +rula-reba, +est, -shared |

**H634 (14-10):** both runs open rula-reba and est (run 2 also reba/components) and then go to source Grep and Glob.

**HORIG (13-05..13-10), uncapped, 12-15 notes per run:**

| Run | Notes opened |
|---|---|
| 1 | reba → reba/components → reba effort-detail, rula → rula/components → rula effort-detail, rula-reba/shared, est, est/components, then shared/services, shared/components, reba and rula score-card, est score-card, screens/report |
| 2 | the same walk, plus `components/inputs` |

HORIG opened truth-bearing notes holding 26 and 27 of the 45 folders. Cap-6 runs got 0, 0 and 11, and cap-3 runs got 0, 6 and 0. The H634 runs got 0 and 6, so six of the seven runs that opened any bearing note did so at cap 6 or lower. H1D6 had zero or 1 bearing notes.

**Where haiku turned off the path:**

- **Parent overview instead of the child note:** 12 of the 18 notes opened in the three cap-6 runs were the parent overviews rula-reba, reba, rula and est. Opening reba/components and the effort-detail notes was never preferred: 2 of 18 cap-6 opens were truth-bearing, and the other 4 were off-path (shared, shared/components, shared/services, screens/report). In cap-3, 7 of 9 opens were parents, 1 was bearing and 1 was off.
- **Parent read, listed child not opened:** this happens in every cap-6 and cap-3 run. In cap-6 runs 1 and 2, reba and rula were read but reba/components and rula/components were not. In all three, est was read but est/components was not, so the est wizard, which holds 6 truth folders, is never reached. Roughly 6-8 truth-bearing notes are listed on a note that was read and then skipped, per run.
- **Sibling or unrelated:** in 4 of 6 cap-6 and cap-3 runs, the remaining cap slots went to `shared/*` and `screens/report`. That is an unrelated pick, not a sibling module.
- **Why this scores as "wrong submodules":** the module metric counts modules named by context Grep hits as selected. In cap-6 run 2 those hits are scoring-models, directives and dialogs, so exact module P is about .06.

**Sonnet V2.1 (6 runs on 6141, F1 .22-.44):**

- It opens 0 or 1 note. In 4 of 6 runs the note is the reba effort-detail note.
- Its first Grep over the context finds about 3-5 hits, mostly just `main`.
- Of 74 truth folders it named, 41 were first surfaced by source Grep, 25 through a note listing, and 8 were never surfaced and appear to be derived from names.
- The source Greps target i18n keys such as `input_type_vision`, `common.(vision|cv)` and `ai_value`, and then the files that use them. That is how it reaches the lateral modules (est cv-backed, ge-adv, lm-*) that the notes do not name.
- So sonnet's advantage on 6141 is source search, not note selection. Reading the effort-detail note is the only note step it takes.

**4. Classification (Stage A and B on 6141, cap-6 plus cap-3, 6 runs, 27 notes opened)**

| Failure | Count |
|---|---|
| Parent-overview opens instead of the child index line (rula-reba, reba, rula, est) | 19 of 27 opens |
| Off-path opens (shared/*, screens/report) | 5 of 27 |
| Truth-bearing note opens | 3 of 27 |

Runs that open the parent overview instead of descending: 6 of 6 (a parent is read and its child is skipped). Runs that open 0 bearing notes: 4 of 6.

HORIG's uncapped walk is parent, then components, then effort-detail, repeated for reba, rula and est. At a cap of 6 that walk stops at the parents. The ticket words do match the deeper index lines, so this is a choice failure, not a visibility failure.

**5. Recommendation**

Two generic prompt changes:

1. **Descend to the deepest matching line.** For each ticket noun, pick the most deeply indented index line whose purpose text mentions it or the feature it names. Open the parent overview only if no child line matches. A product name alone is not a reason to open a parent. Open the deepest matches for each product before any second top-level note. The reason is that the tree already shows the child lines, and each parent costs one of six slots without listing the truth folders.
2. **Follow the listing before leaving a subtree.** After opening a note, if its `## Submodules` list names a child that matches a ticket term, open that child's note before starting another subtree. Never open a cross-cutting `shared` or `screens` note unless a ticket term appears on its index line.

For the second change, any worked example should not use REBA, RULA, EST, wizard or effort-detail. Use an invented tree such as a `parent/child/grandchild` chain over a different domain.

Both changes are enforceable by order and caps, which haiku follows. Haiku obeys the cap of 6 and the opening order. Examples of the first change would still be the wording part, because "pick the deepest" needs a hint on what "matching" means. The second change is a simple ordering rule.

**What this will not fix:**

- The 14 absent folders: 7 manual-override-wizard, 4 lm-lift/lm-lower/lm-carry/rsi effort, 2 display-card and dotted-row, and `ui/tagged-metric`. They are not in any note, so only source Grep reaches them.
- The 6 est wizard folders, which need a 3-deep path through est/components.
- The lateral modules (ge-adv, ui, lm-*), which are found only through the Vision/CV hook.
- A rough ceiling for the change is about 24-26 of 45 folders if reba/components, reba effort-detail, rula/components, rula effort-detail, rula-reba/shared and est/components are the six opens. That is an estimate from the truth map, not a measurement.

| reba and rula `manual-override-wizard/{neck,trunk,lower-arm...}` | 7 | **absent**. The note lists only `manual-override-wizard/`, so these exist only in source. | none |
| rula-reba/shared `display-card`, `dotted-row` | 2 | **absent** from the note (index line exists). Only `models` (1) is listed. | none |
| lm-carry, lm-lift, lm-lower and rsi `manual-override-wizard/effort` | 4 | **absent** from the notes. lm-* have an index line; rsi has none. | none |
| est `score-card/shared/{cv-backed-metric,posture-scale-display}` | 2 | `## Folders` bullet in est/components/score-card (index line) | 1 |
| est wizard folders | 6 | `## Folders` bullet in the est wizard notes. These notes have **no index line**. They are reached through the `## Submodules` list in the est/components overview. | 3 or more (est, est/components, wizard) |
| ge-adv `card-set-display`, `expandable-card-display`, `card-checkbox-set`, `card-radio-button`, `expandable-card-checkbox` | 5 | `## Folders` bullet in a `shared` note (index line) | 1 |
| `components/inputs/cv-backed-form-field`, `ui/card-button`, `ui/tag` | 3 | `## Folders` bullet in an index-line note | 1 |
| `ui/tagged-metric` | 1 | absent from the ui note | none |

Totals: 31 folders are listed as a bullet inside a note (25 in notes with an index line, 6 in the est wizard notes without one). 14 are absent from every note, so no navigation of the context can name them.

**2. Ticket words against index lines**

- **REBA, RULA, EST:** these appear on the product index lines. Examples are "REBA services (API, scoring, forms...) and models", "REBA wizard inputs for neck, trunk, upper and lower arm...", "EST ergonomic screening...", and "Per-effort detail breakdown of REBA scores".
- **"Effort Details":** it maps to the `effort-detail` index lines for reba and rula. Those lines also hold 11 truth folders.
- **"Modal Wizard" and "Single-Page Wizard":** they map to the `components` lines ("wizard inputs"). They do not map to the manual-override-wizard sub-folders, which the notes omit.
- **"Input Type", "Share Report", "Vision/CV", "shorthand", "ai(o)":** none of these appear on a truth-module index line. Only the Vision/CV hook reaches the lateral modules (est cv-backed, ge-adv card sets, lm-*, ui/tag), and only through key symbols such as `ESTCVBackedMetricComponent`.
- **Share Report:** it matches the report-sharing dialogs line, which is off truth.

**3. Haiku and sonnet runs on 6141**

Notation: `+` is a note on a path to truth (an ancestor of a truth folder), `-` is off. The arrow in each Grep entry gives the number of context hits.

**Cap-6, stamp 17-23-05 (F1 .126, .157, .137):**

| Run | Context Grep | Notes opened, in order |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | none | +rula-reba, +est, +reba, +rula, -shared/components, -shared/services |
| 2 | `input type\|input_type\|Input Type\|overridden\|shorthand\|Share Report\|export\|ai\(o\)` → 13 hits, all on scoring-models, directives, models, screens/report, dialogs and nom | +rula-reba, +reba, +rula, +est, -shared, -screens/report |
| 3 | `input.?type\|shorthand\|ai\(o\)\|ai_overridden\|share report\|effort.detail` → 20 hits, including the two effort-detail notes | +rula-reba, +reba, +rula, +est, +reba effort-detail, +rula effort-detail |

All three runs then spent 3-4 source Greps on i18n keys and `isRebaCvChecked`.

**Cap-3, stamp 17-21-02:**

| Run | Context Grep | Notes opened |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `input.?type\|input_indicator\|overrid\|Share Report...` → 53 hits | +reba, +rula, +est |
| 2 | `input type\|overridden\|shorthand\|effort-detail...` → 19 hits, including the effort-detail notes | +rula-reba, +est, +reba effort-detail |
| 3 | none | +rula-reba, +est, -shared |

**H634 (14-10):** both runs open rula-reba and est (run 2 also reba/components) and then go to source Grep and Glob.

**HORIG (13-05..13-10), uncapped, 12-15 notes per run:**

| Run | Notes opened |
|---|---|
| 1 | reba → reba/components → reba effort-detail, rula → rula/components → rula effort-detail, rula-reba/shared, est, est/components, then shared/services, shared/components, reba and rula score-card, est score-card, screens/report |
| 2 | the same walk, plus `components/inputs` |

HORIG opened truth-bearing notes holding 26 and 27 of the 45 folders. Cap-6 runs got 0, 0 and 11, and cap-3 runs got 0, 6 and 0. The H634 runs got 0 and 6, so six of the seven runs that opened any bearing note did so at cap 6 or lower. H1D6 had zero or 1 bearing notes.

**Where haiku turned off the path:**

- **Parent overview instead of the child note:** 12 of the 18 notes opened in the three cap-6 runs were the parent overviews rula-reba, reba, rula and est. Opening reba/components and the effort-detail notes was never preferred: 2 of 18 cap-6 opens were truth-bearing, and the other 4 were off-path (shared, shared/components, shared/services, screens/report). In cap-3, 7 of 9 opens were parents, 1 was bearing and 1 was off.
- **Parent read, listed child not opened:** this happens in every cap-6 and cap-3 run. In cap-6 runs 1 and 2, reba and rula were read but reba/components and rula/components were not. In all three, est was read but est/components was not, so the est wizard, which holds 6 truth folders, is never reached. Roughly 6-8 truth-bearing notes are listed on a note that was read and then skipped, per run.
- **Sibling or unrelated:** in 4 of 6 cap-6 and cap-3 runs, the remaining cap slots went to `shared/*` and `screens/report`. That is an unrelated pick, not a sibling module.
- **Why this scores as "wrong submodules":** the module metric counts modules named by context Grep hits as selected. In cap-6 run 2 those hits are scoring-models, directives and dialogs, so exact module P is about .06.

**Sonnet V2.1 (6 runs on 6141, F1 .22-.44):**

- It opens 0 or 1 note. In 4 of 6 runs the note is the reba effort-detail note.
- Its first Grep over the context finds about 3-5 hits, mostly just `main`.
- Of 74 truth folders it named, 41 were first surfaced by source Grep, 25 through a note listing, and 8 were never surfaced and appear to be derived from names.
- The source Greps target i18n keys such as `input_type_vision`, `common.(vision|cv)` and `ai_value`, and then the files that use them. That is how it reaches the lateral modules (est cv-backed, ge-adv, lm-*) that the notes do not name.
- So sonnet's advantage on 6141 is source search, not note selection. Reading the effort-detail note is the only note step it takes.

**4. Classification (Stage A and B on 6141, cap-6 plus cap-3, 6 runs, 27 notes opened)**

| Failure | Count |
|---|---|
| Parent-overview opens instead of the child index line (rula-reba, reba, rula, est) | 19 of 27 opens |
| Off-path opens (shared/*, screens/report) | 5 of 27 |
| Truth-bearing note opens | 3 of 27 |

Runs that open the parent overview instead of descending: 6 of 6 (a parent is read and its child is skipped). Runs that open 0 bearing notes: 4 of 6.

HORIG's uncapped walk is parent, then components, then effort-detail, repeated for reba, rula and est. At a cap of 6 that walk stops at the parents. The ticket words do match the deeper index lines, so this is a choice failure, not a visibility failure.

**5. Recommendation**

Two generic prompt changes:

1. **Descend to the deepest matching line.** For each ticket noun, pick the most deeply indented index line whose purpose text mentions it or the feature it names. Open the parent overview only if no child line matches. A product name alone is not a reason to open a parent. Open the deepest matches for each product before any second top-level note. The reason is that the tree already shows the child lines, and each parent costs one of six slots without listing the truth folders.
2. **Follow the listing before leaving a subtree.** After opening a note, if its `## Submodules` list names a child that matches a ticket term, open that child's note before starting another subtree. Never open a cross-cutting `shared` or `screens` note unless a ticket term appears on its index line.

For the second change, any worked example should not use REBA, RULA, EST, wizard or effort-detail. Use an invented tree such as a `parent/child/grandchild` chain over a different domain.

Both changes are enforceable by order and caps, which haiku follows. Haiku obeys the cap of 6 and the opening order. Examples of the first change would still be the wording part, because "pick the deepest" needs a hint on what "matching" means. The second change is a simple ordering rule.

**What this will not fix:**

- The 14 absent folders: 7 manual-override-wizard, 4 lm-lift/lm-lower/lm-carry/rsi effort, 2 display-card and dotted-row, and `ui/tagged-metric`. They are not in any note, so only source Grep reaches them.
- The 6 est wizard folders, which need a 3-deep path through est/components.
- The lateral modules (ge-adv, ui, lm-*), which are found only through the Vision/CV hook.
- A rough ceiling for the change is about 24-26 of 45 folders if reba/components, reba effort-detail, rula/components, rula effort-detail, rula-reba/shared and est/components are the six opens. That is an estimate from the truth map, not a measurement.

## Current version

0.6.0 (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, not bumped). Branch `navigator-agent`; commit after every phase/iteration (user, 2026-10-19).
Bench context = `inseer-frontend/.ambicode/context`, backup `.local-docs/context` (never touch; `cmp` index.md after every run).
`node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs` 73 pass, search tests 22 pass, typecheck clean (2026-10-20). `npm run verify` not run since the navigator work.

## Navigator: where we are (2026-10-20)

User decisions: the navigator stays on **haiku** (frequent scope subagent for all skills; a senior model refines; ±0.1 F1 vs sonnet is fine),
packaged as one tool, **no Bash** (too risky). Context exists only to make the navigator faster/cheaper; dropping it is a later decision.
Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plans: parent "navigator eval" (3146e432, phase p11) → child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397, p2 in progress).

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

```
variant                              6141   3571   6404   mean   R mean
bare (sonnet, no context)            .339   .521   .815   .558
sonnet V2.1 (4c6c84ad)               .33    .58    .86    .59
haiku 634cccd3 (cap 3 notes)         .144   .616   .744   .501   .443
haiku + map --folders/--near c46d76ae .050  .374   .738          .427
haiku 634 + map union 3d15eb34       .077   .355   .745          .356
haiku no context 4fef362f            .140   .465   .835   .480   .428
haiku cap 12 notes d5349924          .112   .536   .817   .488   .392
haiku evidence rule, cap 6 4fc7b3f   .140   .537   .815   .497   .447
```

10 cases: bare R .530 P .543 F1 .505 $0.144; sonnet V2 F1 .518; sonnet V2.1 F1 .542 $0.128; context-only sonnet (pre-V2) F1 .396.

### Findings

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.
- Haiku obeys numeric caps and step order (6/6), not floors ("use all N": 3/6) or print steps (0/21). It emits no text/thinking.
- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.
- ~80% of haiku's lost truth folders never appear in a read note; sonnet reaches them by iterating source Greps (~10 on 6141).
- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.
- Bench cost: ~$0.55 per variant (3 cases x3); the sonnet relay main session dominates.

- Evidence-rule variant (129c0ce + cap 6 in 4fc7b3f; current file): "a note line or a Grep hit is evidence", Glob only
  self-composed paths, keep users/used-by, same-kind siblings rule, drop only clearly unrelated, recall framing.
  Funnel moved toward sonnet: named/listed .72 (was .47-.60, sonnet .77); named without source hit .36 (was .09, sonnet .94);
  non-truth kept .21; Glob 0 in 12 runs. F1 flat (mean .497 vs .501): what haiku keeps is now mostly fine, but on 6141 it
  reads the wrong notes (exact module P .06 R .04). Sibling rule followed in 1 of 2 runs that read the sibling note.
  Bench cost ~$0.80 (includes one cap-3 set on 6141: F1 .187).

## Next step

1. 6141 reach: why haiku picks the wrong modules/notes (exact vs related selection) — $0 trace analysis, then one prompt fix.
2. Then: source-search iteration like sonnet (next Grep from the previous hits); decide on the context (user, later).
3. p12: dead code (learn/seed/`navigator` CLI), `npm run verify`, version bump.

## Eval setup (navigator)

- Cases `fe-vs-<id>-navigator`, generated by `evals/scripts/navigator-cases.mjs` (gitignored); never run `evals:generate`
  without `NAV_CASES`/`NAV_BENCH` (it wiped the cases once; regenerated, grader names match for all 10).
- Run: `npm run evals -- --tag navigator --case fe-vs-<id>-navigator --runs N --max-cost-usd X`, one case per command, build first.
- Plugin arm: sonnet relay main session (`allowed_tools: [Agent]`) calls `ambicode:navigator` once. `run.mjs` strips
  `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL*` from the child env (the user's shell forces sonnet otherwise). Scaffold copies context + config.yaml.
- Scoring: truth/answer collapsed to folders, ancestorShare 0.3; metrics in `results/<stamp>/aggregate-result.json`.
- Eval dir must stay under 20,000 entries (18,433 at last count; ~16-30 per case run).
- Bench leakage: inseer-frontend HEAD is after every truth commit (favours source search for all arms).

## Open

- Dead learn/seed code and `navigator` CLI commands in `src/`; USAGE help-line cleanup.
- Path-prefix tolerance in the scorer (bare answers without `main/` score 0) — not decided.
- `skill-content` error-code test on navigator-* codes failing earlier; not checked against unmodified code.

На 6141 haiku тратит лимит заметок на обзоры родительских модулей и не спускается к дочерним, где перечислены нужные папки. Причина в нашем же промпте: в Stage B написано «Open at most 6 notes in total: **the ones for the largest entities**», а Stage A велит упорядочить сущности «from the large to small». Haiku выполняет это буквально.

Какие заметки haiku открывает на 6141 (прогоны с лимитом 3 и 6, всего 6 прогонов и 27 открытий):

```
обзор родителя (rula-reba, reba, rula, est)          19 / 27
мимо (shared/*, screens/report)                        5 / 27
заметка, где перечислены нужные папки                  3 / 27
прогонов, где ни одной такой заметки                   4 / 6
```

- **Родитель прочитан, дочерняя пропущена — в каждом из 6 прогонов.** Например, прочитан `est`, но не `est/components`. Слова тикета («Effort Details», REBA, RULA, EST) совпадают как раз с более глубокими строками индекса. Значит, это ошибка выбора, а не того, что контекст не показывает нужное.
- **Без лимита haiku доходил до нужного.** Он шёл родитель → components → effort-detail и открывал заметки, где перечислены 26 из 45 нужных папок.
- **Sonnet открывает одну заметку, нужную (effort-detail).** Дальше он ищет по коду: 41 из 74 названных им нужных папок пришли из поиска.
- **14 из 45 нужных папок нет ни в одной заметке.** До них дойдёт только поиск по коду, эта правка их не закроет.

**Правка, одна по смыслу:**
1. В Stage B заменить «the ones for the largest entities» на: «the most specific ones: for each ticket term, the deepest index line whose text matches it; open a parent overview only when no child line matches».
2. Из Stage A убрать порядок «from the large to small».
3. Добавить правило порядка: если в открытой заметке в `## Submodules` есть дочерний модуль, совпадающий с термином тикета, открыть его раньше, чем начинать другое поддерево.

Haiku соблюдает порядок и лимиты, так что это должно сработать. Пример, если понадобится, сделаю на выдуманном дереве, не похожем на бенч.

Бенч: 6141, 3571 и 6404 по 3 прогона, около $0.55. На 6141 разбор оценивает потолок примерно в 24–26 из 45 папок, если haiku откроет правильные шесть заметок. Это оценка по карте, не замер. Делать?

  **2. Ticket words against index lines**
  
  - **REBA, RULA, EST:** these appear on the product index lines. Examples are "REBA services (API, scoring, forms...) and models", "REBA wizard inputs for neck, trunk, upper and lower arm...", "EST ergonomic screening...", and "Per-effort detail breakdown of REBA scores".

На 6141 haiku тратит лимит заметок на обзоры родительских модулей и не спускается к дочерним, где перечислены нужные папки. Причина в нашем же промпте: в Stage B написано «Open at most 6 notes in total: **the ones for the largest entities**», а Stage A велит упорядочить сущности «from the large to small». Haiku выполняет это буквально.

Какие заметки haiku открывает на 6141 (прогоны с лимитом 3 и 6, всего 6 прогонов и 27 открытий):

```
обзор родителя (rula-reba, reba, rula, est)          19 / 27
мимо (shared/*, screens/report)                        5 / 27
заметка, где перечислены нужные папки                  3 / 27
прогонов, где ни одной такой заметки                   4 / 6
```

- **Родитель прочитан, дочерняя пропущена — в каждом из 6 прогонов.** Например, прочитан `est`, но не `est/components`. Слова тикета («Effort Details», REBA, RULA, EST) совпадают как раз с более глубокими строками индекса. Значит, это ошибка выбора, а не того, что контекст не показывает нужное.
- **Без лимита haiku доходил до нужного.** Он шёл родитель → components → effort-detail и открывал заметки, где перечислены 26 из 45 нужных папок.
- **Sonnet открывает одну заметку, нужную (effort-detail).** Дальше он ищет по коду: 41 из 74 названных им нужных папок пришли из поиска.
- **14 из 45 нужных папок нет ни в одной заметке.** До них дойдёт только поиск по коду, эта правка их не закроет.

**Правка, одна по смыслу:**
1. В Stage B заменить «the ones for the largest entities» на: «the most specific ones: for each ticket term, the deepest index line whose text matches it; open a parent overview only when no child line matches».
2. Из Stage A убрать порядок «from the large to small».
3. Добавить правило порядка: если в открытой заметке в `## Submodules` есть дочерний модуль, совпадающий с термином тикета, открыть его раньше, чем начинать другое поддерево.

Haiku соблюдает порядок и лимиты, так что это должно сработать. Пример, если понадобится, сделаю на выдуманном дереве, не похожем на бенч.

Бенч: 6141, 3571 и 6404 по 3 прогона, около $0.55. На 6141 разбор оценивает потолок примерно в 24–26 из 45 папок, если haiku откроет правильные шесть заметок. Это оценка по карте, не замер. Делать?

description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob

You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself: it drops an extra path in a second, but it never finds a path you left out. When unsure, keep the path. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Order the list broad from the large to small entities: app, module, service, controller, model, value. Inside a group the most ticked related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 6 notes in total: the ones for the largest entities. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note keep every source the ticket changes, and every source that uses or is used by what it changes. A note line naming a path is evidence enough: it needs no Grep or Glob to count.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Keep same-kind siblings. When you keep one subfolder of a kind (one per item, field, variant or step), keep every sibling of that kind the note lists, unless the ticket excludes it.
   Example: the ticket renames the toggle label in every notification setting; `settings/` lists `email-row/`, `sms-row/`, `push-row/`, `profile/`. Answer all three `*-row/` folders, not only the one a Grep hit.
7. Drop only paths that are clearly unrelated to the ticket. When unsure, keep the path.

2. For each shared piece in the scope that other code uses (a component selector, a guard, a directive, a constant, a model field the ticket changes), Grep its name once and add the consumer folders the ticket changes. One hop only.

### Findings

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.

- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.
- ~80% of haiku's lost truth folders never appear in a read note; sonnet reaches them by iterating source Greps (~10 on 6141).
- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.
- Bench cost: ~$0.55 per variant (3 cases x3); the sonnet relay main session dominates.

- Evidence-rule variant (129c0ce + cap 6 in 4fc7b3f; current file): "a note line or a Grep hit is evidence", Glob only
  self-composed paths, keep users/used-by, same-kind siblings rule, drop only clearly unrelated, recall framing.
  Funnel moved toward sonnet: named/listed .72 (was .47-.60, sonnet .77); named without source hit .36 (was .09, sonnet .94);

message.content: как он читает заметки и код?

content.text:
Заметки haiku читает целиком, по шагам промпта. Код он почти не читает: видит только пути файлов, которые вернул Grep.

**Заметки.** `index.md` читается один раз целиком. Потом haiku открывает до 6 заметок через Read, тоже целиком, как велит B1 («read it whole»). Пути он берёт из списков `## Folders` и `## Submodules` и из ключевых файлов в заметке. Grep по контексту делает 0–2 раза на прогон: ищет слова тикета, которых нет в индексе. Совпавшая строка `## Folders` считается входом в индекс.

**Код.** По последнему бенчу на прогон:

```
              src Grep   Glob   Read исходников
6141            2–3       0          0
3571            1–3       0          0
6404            2–4       0          0
```

- Grep идёт в режиме `files_with_matches`, как требует Stage C. Значит, haiku получает только список файлов, где есть совпадение, без строк кода.
- Исходники он не открывает: ни одного Read в 9 прогонах. Единственный Read исходника был в одном прогоне прошлого варианта.
- Glob после правила доказательства пропал совсем.

Получается, о коде haiku знает только две вещи: пути из заметок и имена файлов, где нашёлся Grep. Что внутри файла, какие у него импорты и кто его использует, он не видит.

**Sonnet работает иначе.** Он открывает 0–1 заметку и делает около 10 Grep на 6141. Ищет по ключам и символам: `input_type_vision`, `common.(vision|cv)`. Потом ищет, какие файлы их используют. 41 из 74 нужных папок, которые он назвал, пришли именно из поиска. Режим вывода его Grep (строки или только файлы) я отдельно не проверял.

**Не проверено.** Читает ли haiku заметки действительно целиком или с `offset/limit`. И не обрезает ли длинные заметки лимит Read. Это можно бесплатно проверить по параметрам вызовов в трейсах.

Отсюда возможный рычаг для 6141 и тех 14 папок, которых нет в заметках. Один Grep в режиме `content` по найденному символу и один следующий Grep по тому, что нашлось в строках. То есть переход «символ → его использование», как у sonnet. Это задаётся порядком и числом вызовов, которые haiku соблюдает. Но сначала, по плану, подтверждение на 10 кейсах.

Заметки haiku читает целиком, по шагам промпта. Код он почти не читает: видит только пути файлов, которые вернул Grep.

**Заметки.** `index.md` читается один раз целиком. Потом haiku открывает до 6 заметок через Read, тоже целиком, как велит B1 («read it whole»). Пути он берёт из списков `## Folders` и `## Submodules` и из ключевых файлов в заметке. Grep по контексту делает 0–2 раза на прогон: ищет слова тикета, которых нет в индексе. Совпавшая строка `## Folders` считается входом в индекс.

**Код.** По последнему бенчу на прогон:

```
              src Grep   Glob   Read исходников
6141            2–3       0          0
3571            1–3       0          0
6404            2–4       0          0
```

- Grep идёт в режиме `files_with_matches`, как требует Stage C. Значит, haiku получает только список файлов, где есть совпадение, без строк кода.
- Исходники он не открывает: ни одного Read в 9 прогонах. Единственный Read исходника был в одном прогоне прошлого варианта.
- Glob после правила доказательства пропал совсем.

Получается, о коде haiku знает только две вещи: пути из заметок и имена файлов, где нашёлся Grep. Что внутри файла, какие у него импорты и кто его использует, он не видит.

**Sonnet работает иначе.** Он открывает 0–1 заметку и делает около 10 Grep на 6141. Ищет по ключам и символам: `input_type_vision`, `common.(vision|cv)`. Потом ищет, какие файлы их используют. 41 из 74 нужных папок, которые он назвал, пришли именно из поиска. Режим вывода его Grep (строки или только файлы) я отдельно не проверял.

**Не проверено.** Читает ли haiku заметки действительно целиком или с `offset/limit`. И не обрезает ли длинные заметки лимит Read. Это можно бесплатно проверить по параметрам вызовов в трейсах.

Отсюда возможный рычаг для 6141 и тех 14 папок, которых нет в заметках. Один Grep в режиме `content` по найденному символу и один следующий Grep по тому, что нашлось в строках. Прирост подтвердился на 10 кейсах. Haiku-навигатор (`932b65e4`) обходит bare и sonnet V2.1 по F1 и стоит втрое дешевле.

```
10 кейсов     R     P     F1    $/прогон
haiku x3    .593  .610  .572  .054
sonnet V2.1 .493  .662  .542  .128   (x2)
bare x3     .530  .543  .505  .144
```

По кейсам (F1):

```
кейс    438  6141 5948 6292 5967 5164 6404 3571 6406 6086
haiku  .470 .194 .517 .473 .766 .857 .852 .555 .610 .431
bare   .738 .339 .502 .159 .503 .589 .815 .521 .480 .400
V2.1   .500 .331 .499 .309 .514 .803 .833 .520 .500 .615
```

- **Против bare:** выше в 8 кейсах из 10. Ниже на 438 (−.27) и 6141 (−.15).
- **Против V2.1:** ниже на 6086 (−.18), 6141 (−.14) и 438 (−.03), в остальных семи выше.
- **Слабые места:**
  - **6141:** recall .185, всё ещё теряем найденное при именовании.
  - **438:** recall .833, но precision .329, ответ слишком широкий. Один из трёх прогонов дал .25.
  - **6086:** заметно хуже, чем у sonnet.
- **Проверки прогона:** все 30 прогонов прошли без нулевых скоров и ошибок. Все ходы навигатора шли на haiku. Индекс бенча совпадает с бэкапом. В каталоге eval 18 705 записей, предел 20 000 не перейдён. Прогон стоил $1.61.

Цель дочернего плана выполнена: recall ≥ .50 при стоимости уровня haiku. Фаза p4 закрыта, результаты записаны в план и в STATE.md. Сам навигатор я не менял, так что коммитить нечего: проверялся уже закоммиченный `932b65e4`.

Следующий шаг я пока не запускал. Предлагаю такой:
- **6141:** добавить в Stage C один content-mode Grep по найденному символу и затем один переход к его использованиям, как это делает sonnet. Так мы доберёмся до 14 из 45 нужных папок, которых нет ни в одной заметке.
- **438 и 6086:** параллельно разобрать трассы и сравнить их с V2.1, это бесплатно.

Проверять изменение будем бенчем 3 кейса ×3, это около $0.55. Запускать?

## 2026-10-17 Navigator
1. **Standalone agent, evaluated against bare only.** Why: the old insertion broke routes (a confident map skipped it and fenced the model; always-on doubled investigate cost). Rejected: route insertion / calls from investigate and plan.
2. **Feature-oriented map in `.ambicode/navigator/features.md`, separate from `context/`.** Entry: feature, terms, files, deps, models. Why: a prompt often does not name its feature, so term-to-path lookups miss it. Budget 2500 tokens (chars/4), at most 30 entries of 80 tokens (user set 2026-10-17, was 2000). Rejected: per-module `## Keywords` (0 recall gain twice), flat term-to-path list.
3. **Learning (step 4) kept and tested.** Why: the user's case ("fix modal for location for user migration") shows grep cannot find unnamed features. Rejected: ship without step 4.
4. **Fixtures derived from the 20 real NDA nav cases stay local** (outside committed files). Rejected: committing them.
5. **`harvest` ecosystem patterns (`DECLARATION_PATTERNS`) deferred.** Why: no failure observed. Revisit only if it fails.
6. **Navigator eval runs one case at a time with map copy-back.** Why: a symlink to the persistent map was EPERM in the sandbox. Rejected: symlinked map.
7. **Navigator results merged into `results/<arm>.json`; navigator excluded from the default suite run (`--tag navigator` only).** Why: it is costly and has its own bench.
8. **Map = directory index (hierarchy + flat by file count) + learned entries in one 2500-token budget.** Index <=900 tokens generated by `navigator seed`, `# Learned` entries (max 20) written only by `navigator learn`, which never touches the Index and evicts the oldest learned entries. Why: the cap-driven seed folded directories under 46 files and hid sibling/feature dirs (bench: 1779 files, niosh/rsi/lm-* gone, names only last segment). Rejected: one entry per feature dir (~3400 tokens, needs depth detection), bigger budget.

## 2026-10-19 Navigator eval levers (offline simulation, share 0.3; plugin F1 0.416, bare 0.525 under the sim scorer)
9. **Ship d-path: resolve each answer path against the repo, strip an invented leading prefix, drop `*.md` and paths that do not exist.** Why: leak-free, no greps, +0.016 suite F1 and +0.04 bench F1 (mostly the `src/app/` prefix in 6141). Rejected, because they add recall but lose more precision or gain only from leakage of the post-change HEAD tree: mechanical usage-hop top-K (F1 0.336–0.392), git co-change (0.400), ticket-term grep union (0.417 → 0.382 leak-free), leaf refine by grep hits (0.450/0.453 → 0.434/0.423 leak-free).

11. **Bench validity issue: `inseer-frontend` HEAD is after every truth commit.** The sandbox tree and the context both contain the solution, which favors source search for both arms. 17 truth folders also do not exist at HEAD. Open: user decision.

## Current version

0.6.0 (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, not bumped). Branch `navigator-agent`; commit after every phase/iteration (user, 2026-10-19).
Bench context = `inseer-frontend/.ambicode/context`, backup `.local-docs/context` (never touch; `cmp` index.md after every run).
`node --test evals/scripts/*.test.mjs` 73 pass, search tests 22 pass, typecheck clean (2026-10-20). `npm run verify` not run since the navigator work.

## Navigator: where we are (2026-10-20)

User decisions: the navigator stays on **haiku** (frequent scope subagent for all skills; a senior model refines; ±0.1 F1 vs sonnet is fine),
packaged as one tool, **no Bash** (too risky). Context exists only to make the navigator faster/cheaper; dropping it is a later decision.
Main problem now: **haiku cuts its own findings**.

Active plans: parent "navigator eval" (3146e432, phase p11) → child "haiku navigator + map tool" (540d2397, p1-p4 done).

### Bench: 6141 / 3571 / 6404, F1 (haiku unless noted; x2-x3 runs, haiku variance about ±0.15)

```
variant                              6141   3571   6404   mean   R mean
bare (sonnet, no context)            .339   .521   .815   .558
sonnet V2.1 (4c6c84ad)               .33    .58    .86    .59
haiku 634cccd3 (cap 3 notes)         .144   .616   .744   .501   .443
haiku + map --folders/--near c46d76ae .050  .374   .738          .427
haiku 634 + map union 3d15eb34       .077   .355   .745          .356
haiku no context 4fef362f            .140   .465   .835   .480   .428
haiku cap 12 notes d5349924          .112   .536   .817   .488   .392
haiku evidence rule, cap 6 4fc7b3f   .140   .537   .815   .497   .447
haiku deepest notes 932b65e4         .185   .625   .815   .542   .503   <- current file
```

10 cases: bare R .530 P .543 F1 .505 $0.144; sonnet V2 F1 .518; sonnet V2.1 F1 .542 $0.128; context-only sonnet (pre-V2) F1 .396.
**haiku 932b65e4, 10x3 (2026-10-20, stamps 17-55-29..18-12-57): R .593 P .610 F1 .572 $0.054/run** ($1.61 total, 0 zero-score).

```
case   438  6141 5948 6292 5967 5164 6404 3571 6406 6086
haiku .470 .194 .517 .473 .766 .857 .852 .555 .610 .431
bare  .738 .339 .502 .159 .503 .589 .815 .521 .480 .400
V2.1  .500 .331 .499 .309 .514 .803 .833 .520 .500 .615
```
Weak: 6141 (R .185), 438 (R .833 but P .329, per-run .55/.62/.25), 6086 (vs V2.1 -.18). Haiku peak context ~25k, 7.6 tool calls/run.

- Bash variants failed because granting Bash removed Grep/Glob from the subagent (`No such tool available: Grep`); reverted
  (`e12562fe`), `map --folders/--near` removed (`5ffc1b3f`). Offline data-file (i18n key) hop: no gain.
- Haiku obeys numeric caps and step order (6/6), not floors ("use all N": 3/6) or print steps (0/21). It emits no text/thinking.
- Stage A: haiku selects modules as well as sonnet (related-module R .73-.88 vs .58).
- Funnel: truth folders listed in a read note, named: haiku .40-.64, sonnet .77. Named without a source hit: haiku .08-.09,
  sonnet .94. Haiku names only what Grep/Glob returned ("not globbed, so they are left out") → the "confirmed" answer rule.
- ~80% of haiku's lost truth folders never appear in a read note; sonnet reaches them by iterating source Greps (~10 on 6141).
- Context: no measurable gain on haiku (no-context .480 vs .501), doubles peak context (8-19k vs 22-37k). No-ctx ablation for
  sonnet not run.
- Bench cost: ~$0.55 per variant (3 cases x3); the sonnet relay main session dominates.

- Evidence-rule variant (129c0ce + cap 6 in 4fc7b3f; current file): "a note line or a Grep hit is evidence", Glob only
  self-composed paths, keep users/used-by, same-kind siblings rule, drop only clearly unrelated, recall framing.
  Funnel moved toward sonnet: named/listed .72 (was .47-.60, sonnet .77); named without source hit .36 (was .09, sonnet .94);
  non-truth kept .21; Glob 0 in 12 runs. F1 flat (mean .497 vs .501): what haiku keeps is now mostly fine, but on 6141 it
  reads the wrong notes (exact module P .06 R .04). Sibling rule followed in 1 of 2 runs that read the sibling note.
  Bench cost ~$0.80 (includes one cap-3 set on 6141: F1 .187).

content.content:
---
name: navigator
description: Use proactively, before any manual grep or file search, whenever a task or ticket (a bug, feature, copy or UI change) must be mapped to the files it touches in an unfamiliar repository. Give it the task as free text; it returns the list of files to change, with a reason for each.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob
model: haiku
---
You map a free-text ticket to the SCOPE of the code it's related to: source files. A planner works after you and opens the code itself: it drops an extra path in a second, but it never finds a path you left out. When unsure, keep the path. Do not call any tool before you finish with **Stage A**.

## What you can read

`.ambicode/context/` is your map: `index.md` and the notes it links (overview.md, modules/**). Start there (Stages A and B). Source files are searched only in **Stage C**, to find what the notes do not show. A folder line's text in `index.md` is relative to the folder line above it; its full path is its link target without the leading `modules/` and the trailing `/overview.md` or `.md`, and answers use full repo paths.

## Stage A: entities (before any tool call except reading index.md)

Read entire `index.md` once. And find the modules, that are related to the task. The index lists modules only; the notes' `## Folders` lists name many more folders. For the keywords the index does not match, Grep the whole context folder (one alternation pattern per group of keywords, at most 3 Greps) and treat a matching `## Folders` line as an index entry of its note.

Then, from collected data, create the list of every project-related entity the ticket mentions or implies:  modules, services, controllers, models, constants, values, configs.

Match each entity to the deepest index line whose text names it or the feature it belongs to; a product or area name alone does not make its top-level line the match when a line below it fits better. Most ticket-related first. Print in the format:

`<task wording> | <deepest index entry it matches, or "not in index"> | <key words>`

Follow those matches to identify the scope the ticket belongs and find the rest of related sources in **Stage B**

## Stage B: notes

Go through the list top to bottom and read all index entries in a bulk. Open at most 6 notes in total: the most specific ones, the deepest matching index lines from Stage A. Open a parent overview only when no line below it matches the ticket. Find everything else by source search in Stage C.

1. For an entity with an index entry, open the note the entry links to (the `[dir](path/overview.md)` link) and read it whole.
2. From the note keep every source the ticket changes, and every source that uses or is used by what it changes. A note line naming a path is evidence enough: it needs no Grep or Glob to count.
3. If the note has a dependency that related to the task, read dependency's note too. And a task related references relied on ths. No further.
4. Never open the same note twice. Never enter a folder's note a second time. When an opened note's `## Submodules` names a child that matches a ticket term, open that child's note before a note from another part of the tree.
5. Refine the scope. A folder whose note lists subfolders (`## Folders` or `## Submodules`) is too broad to answer: replace it with only the subfolders the ticket touches, named from that note, plus its own files that the ticket touches. Repeat until every folder left has no subfolder the ticket does not touch.
   Example: the ticket changes a label on the chart tooltips; `reports/` lists `charts/`, `export/`, `summary/`; `reports/charts/` lists `tooltip/`, `legend/`, `axis/`. Answer `reports/charts/tooltip/`, not `reports/` or `reports/charts/`.
6. Keep same-kind siblings. When you keep one subfolder of a kind (one per item, field, variant or step), keep every sibling of that kind the note lists, unless the ticket excludes it.
   Example: the ticket renames the toggle label in every notification setting; `settings/` lists `email-row/`, `sms-row/`, `push-row/`, `profile/`. Answer all three `*-row/` folders, not only the one a Grep hit.
7. Drop only paths that are clearly unrelated to the ticket. When unsure, keep the path.

## Stage C: source search (at most 6 Greps)

message names the pack and the reason. Changing it is a deliberate edit to that
pack's `commandPolicy`, not something to work around.
